name: DorkAgent
description: 🤖 LLM-powered agent for automated Google Dorking in bug hunting & pentesting.

name: council-of-high-intelligence
description: Structured multi-perspective deliberation for hard decisions. Run full councils, focused triads, or duo debates across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.

name: openclaw-api-list
description: OpenClaw API Directory: 10,000+ APIs organized for OpenClaw. Maintained by The Operator Vault.
analysis: openclaw-api-list is a curated directory of over 10,000 third-party APIs organized into category folders (agents, AI, automation, developer tools, ecommerce, lead-generation, MCP servers, social media, etc.), each with its own README, purpose-built for wiring integrations into the OpenClaw agent framework. It includes scripts for fetching Apify actors and generating the README indexes, plus a promotional 'Operator Vault' membership page, suggesting it's maintained as a lead-gen/reference resource rather than an actively curated community list. Useful mainly as a browsable catalog of connector candidates for OpenClaw-based automations; it has seen no updates since shortly after creation.

use_cases.title: Find a third-party API to wire into an OpenClaw automation
Browse MCP server APIs organized by category
Locate lead-generation or ecommerce APIs for an integration

name: skills
description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
analysis: Matt Pocock's personal, heavily-starred collection of AI-agent engineering skills ('Skills for Real Engineers') covering requirement-gathering interviews (grill-me), domain-modeling/shared-language docs, spec-to-tickets breakdown, TDD, debugging, and codebase-architecture review, designed to be small, composable, and model-agnostic rather than owning the whole dev process like GSD, BMAD, or Spec-Kit. Distributed as a Claude Code plugin (managed, read-only) or via the skills.sh installer (editable copies) for Codex and other agents; splits skills into user-invoked (slash commands) versus model-invoked (auto-triggered) categories.

use_cases.title: Run a grilling interview to align an agent on unclear requirements
Break a plan or spec into dependency-ordered tracer-bullet tickets
Drive red-green-refactor TDD from an agent skill
Survey a codebase for architecture-deepening opportunities

name: open-seo
description: Open source alternative to Semrush and Ahrefs
analysis: OpenSEO is an open-source, self-hostable alternative to Semrush/Ahrefs for keyword research, rank tracking, competitor and backlink analysis, and site audits, built on a pay-as-you-go DataForSEO API key rather than a subscription. It ships a modern TypeScript web UI plus an MCP server and a library of pre-built AI agent skills (keyword research, competitor analysis, site audit, etc.) so tools like Claude Code can drive SEO workflows directly. Aimed at solo operators and small teams who find commercial SEO suites too expensive or bloated and want to self-host or fork a leaner tool.

use_cases.title: Self-host an SEO suite instead of paying for Semrush/Ahrefs
Let an AI agent run keyword research and site audits
Track competitor backlinks and rankings
Fork and customize an SEO tool's workflows

note: Reviewed. Intended use: build the search-engine-optimization plan for dexevo-site-travel (keyword research, rank tracking, site audit) — self-hosted Semrush/Ahrefs alternative.

name: unsloth
description: Local UI to run and train LLMs and diffusion models, including Qwen3.8, Kimi K3, MiniMax-H3, Gemma 4, DeepSeek-V4, FLUX and more.
analysis: Unsloth has grown from a fine-tuning acceleration library into a full local-first desktop app (Tauri-based Unsloth Desktop plus a web-based Unsloth Studio and a code-based Unsloth Core) for running, training, and deploying LLMs, diffusion, embedding, and audio models such as Kimi K3, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek-V4, Gemma 4, and FLUX. It supports 2x faster/70% less VRAM LoRA/QLoRA/full fine-tuning, RL (GRPO/DPO), GGUF/NVFP4/FP8 export, an OpenAI-compatible serving API, remote access via Cloudflare tunnels, and integration as a local model backend for Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents via MCP. It targets ML practitioners and hobbyists who want to fine-tune and self-host open models across CPU/NVIDIA/AMD/Intel/Apple Silicon hardware.

use_cases.title: Fine-tune an open LLM with LoRA/QLoRA on consumer GPU hardware
Run a local desktop app to chat with and train open-weight models
Connect a locally fine-tuned model to Claude Code or Codex as a subagent
Export a fine-tuned model to GGUF or FP8 for deployment

name: HEAVEN-Autonomous-Penetration-Testing
description: ☠️ A production-grade autonomous penetration testing platform that automates deep reconnaissance, machine learning-driven risk scoring, verified exploitation, and compliance reporting. Features 172 modules, an async task graph orchestrator, and automated threat mapping to MITRE ATT&CK and OWASP Top 10.
analysis: HEAVEN is a production-grade autonomous penetration-testing platform written primarily in Python/FastAPI that automates reconnaissance, vulnerability detection, verified exploitation, post-exploitation, and compliance reporting, usable via a 55-command CLI, a 25-page React web UI, or a 77-route RBAC REST/WebSocket API. It combines classical security tooling (nmap, sqlmap, Nuclei, GTFOBins-based privesc engines) with an LLM observe-plan-act loop (Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini, or a deterministic no-API-key fallback) for recon planning, attack-chain building, and false-positive review, plus a CVSS ML risk predictor and MITRE ATT&CK/kill-chain mapping. It targets professional penetration testers and red teams who want to automate the repeatable parts of an authorized engagement while retaining human judgment for exploitation decisions, and ships with Docker/Helm deployment and an extensive test suite.

use_cases.title: Run an automated recon-to-report pentest engagement from the CLI in CI
Triage and prioritize findings with an ML-based CVSS risk predictor
Map discovered vulnerabilities to MITRE ATT&CK techniques for a compliance report
Drive a bug-bounty or CTF engagement through a web dashboard with live findings

name: Wan2GP
description: A fast AI Video Generator for the GPU Poor. Supports Wan 2.1/2.2, LTX-2, Qwen Image, Hunyuan Video, LTX  Video and Flux.
analysis: WanGP (Wan2GP) is a fast, actively developed all-in-one generative media app for GPU-constrained users, wrapping many open-source video (Wan, LTX-2, Hunyuan Video, LongCat), image (Qwen Image, Flux, HiDream), and audio/TTS (Ace Step, Qwen3 TTS, Chatterbox) models behind one web UI. It supports low-VRAM setups (as little as 6GB), older and AMD GPUs, LoRA customization, quantized checkpoints (int8/fp8/GGUF/NVFP4), a generation queue, headless batch mode, and an API for embedding generation into other apps. An extremely active project with frequent weekly releases and a large Discord community, aimed at hobbyists and builders who want broad open-source model coverage without high-end hardware.

use_cases.title: Generate AI video, image, or audio on a low-VRAM or older GPU
Run a queued batch of generation jobs headlessly
Add generative video/image/audio capability to your own app via API
Apply LoRAs across many open-source video and image models

name: PokeTokenBar
description: Use your tokens to raise, evolve, and collect Pokémon! 🥚
analysis: PokeTokenBar is a native Swift/SwiftUI macOS menu-bar app that gamifies AI coding token usage: it reads local usage logs from Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cursor, and several other CLIs, and turns tokens spent into a growing, hatching, evolving Pokémon companion with a Pokédex, shop, and rare-candy economy, on top of a genuine usage/cost/rate-limit tracker. All data is read locally from each tool's own log files with no external usage CLI required. It targets developers who use multiple AI coding CLIs and want a more engaging way to monitor token spend and rate limits than a plain dashboard.

use_cases.title: Track daily/weekly Claude Code or Codex token usage from the macOS menu bar
Gamify AI coding usage by hatching and evolving a Pokémon companion
Get burn-rate forecasts and alerts before hitting 5-hour/weekly rate limits

name: cloudflare-os
description: Agent workspace built on Cloudflare Workers for creating documents, building apps, and running agents with your company’s context and systems.
analysis: Cloudflare OS is an open-source 'operating system' for AI productivity: an agent chat UI that spins up sandboxed, per-user application instances ('Gadgets') on demand, secured by a capability-based access layer called Gatekeepers that mediates agent access to external services with asynchronous human-in-the-loop approval. Built on Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, and Dynamic Workers by the Workers team itself, it's meant for companies to fork and rebrand as their own internal AI platform. It's explicitly early access / heavy development (v2 rewrite) but backed by Cloudflare and used internally at the company.

use_cases.title: Stand up a self-hosted AI productivity workspace for a company
Build sandboxed AI-generated mini apps ('gadgets')
Study capability-based security patterns for agent tool access

name: multica
description: Assign issues to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and 17 more coding agents like teammates — open-source and self-hostable.
analysis: Multica is a self-hostable, Kanban-style workspace where AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and 17 more CLIs) are added as teammates, assigned issues, and picked up automatically on a daemon-controlled runtime, reporting progress, raising blockers, and handing work back for human review as a PR. It has a Next.js web frontend, Go/Chi backend with PostgreSQL+pgvector, Electron desktop apps for macOS/Windows/Linux, an Expo iOS app, and integrations with GitHub/GitLab/Gitea, Slack/Lark/DingTalk/WeCom, plus 'squads' mixing agents and people and 'autopilots' for cron-scheduled agent runs. Aimed at teams or solo builders who want to run many different coding-agent CLIs against real issues with an execution log, review gates, and cost tracking.

use_cases.title: Assign a GitHub issue to Claude Code or Codex as if it were a teammate
Self-host a board that drives 20 different coding-agent CLIs
Track token cost and execution logs per agent run
Run scheduled agent standups or audits via autopilots

name: OpenSandbox
description: Secure, Fast, and Extensible Sandbox runtime for AI agents.
analysis: OpenSandbox is a general-purpose sandbox runtime for AI applications, providing multi-language SDKs (Python, Java/Kotlin, TypeScript, C#, Go), a CLI (osb), and an MCP server for creating isolated sandboxes and running commands, file I/O, and code execution. It runs on Docker or Kubernetes with strong-isolation runtimes like gVisor, Kata, and Firecracker, a credential vault for safe outbound secrets, and an ingress/egress network policy layer, targeting teams that need to safely execute untrusted code from coding agents, browser-automation agents, or RL training loops at scale. Backed by Alibaba and listed in the CNCF landscape, with examples for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, LangGraph, and Playwright sandboxes.

use_cases.title: Run untrusted AI-agent-generated code in an isolated sandbox
Give a coding agent like Claude Code a disposable sandbox via MCP
Scale sandbox workloads on Kubernetes for RL training or evaluation

name: orca
description: Orca is the ADE for working with a fleet of parallel agents. Run any coding agent with your own subscription. Available on desktop, mobile and VPS.
analysis: Orca is a YC-backed 'agent IDE' (ADE) desktop app for running many coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, and more) in parallel, each in its own isolated git worktree, with a Ghostty-class terminal, SSH remote worktrees, a mobile companion app for monitoring/steering agents remotely, GitHub/Linear integration, and a scriptable CLI. Targets developers running fleets of parallel AI coding agents who need to compare and merge results, on macOS/Windows/Linux plus iOS/Android.

use_cases.title: Run five coding agents in parallel worktrees and merge the best result
Monitor and steer a running coding agent from a phone
Run a coding agent on a remote box over SSH with full terminal access
Script agent workflows from the CLI, e.g. create worktree, snapshot, click

name: Rockxy
description: Open-source native macOS HTTP debugging proxy — intercept HTTPS, inspect APIs, mock responses, debug WebSocket & GraphQL. Community-driven. For developers, by developers.
analysis: Rockxy is a native macOS Swift application that acts as an HTTP/HTTPS/WebSocket/GraphQL debugging proxy, positioned as an open-source (AGPL Community edition) alternative to Proxyman and Charles Proxy. It offers traffic capture and inspection, advanced filtering, TLS certificate management, map-local/map-remote, block/bypass lists, a built-in AI assistant (local analysis plus optional Ollama or cloud providers) for investigating captured traffic, and a local MCP server exposing ten read-only tools so Claude Desktop or Cursor can query captured traffic directly. It targets iOS/API/backend developers debugging network traffic on a Mac who want a trustworthy, inspectable, locally-run proxy tool.

use_cases.title: Intercept and inspect HTTPS traffic from an iOS app or Mac process
Ask an AI assistant to explain why a captured API call failed
Query captured network traffic from Claude Desktop or Cursor via MCP
Mock or redirect a flaky third-party API with Map Local/Map Remote

name: hivemind
description: Hivemind turns your traces into reusable skills across agents
analysis: Hivemind is a cloud-backed shared-memory service (from Activeloop/Deeplake) that captures every coding-agent session's prompts, tool calls, and responses as structured traces, then mines them into reusable SKILL.md files that propagate across every agent on a team. It installs via a single npm command and wires hooks/MCP/plugins into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes, pi, and Claude Cowork, with hybrid lexical+semantic search over traces and skills, BYOC storage (GCS/Azure/S3/on-prem), and session summarization into wiki pages. Aimed at teams who want a single 'brain' so one engineer's fix becomes every agent's capability, with published LoCoMo benchmark numbers showing cost/token/turn reductions versus no shared memory.

use_cases.title: Share one memory brain across a team's coding agents
Auto-generate reusable SKILL.md files from agent traces
Search past agent sessions with hybrid lexical and semantic retrieval
Bring your own cloud storage for captured agent session data

name: openreply
description: Open-source ManyChat alternative: comment-dm automation + account analytics. NOTE: the link below will not allow you to OAuth; you must self-host with your own API keys.
analysis: OpenReply is a self-hosted, open-source alternative to ManyChat for Instagram comment-to-DM automation: when a comment matches a keyword, it sends the commenter a private reply via Meta's official Instagram API, with optional public replies, tracked links, follow gates, and per-account rate limiting. Built on Next.js, Prisma/PostgreSQL, and BullMQ/Redis with a separate worker process for sending, it targets creators and small agencies who want ManyChat-style comment automation without a recurring subscription or seat limits. It uses only the official Meta API (no scraping or password use) and includes multi-account workspaces with roles for agency use.

use_cases.title: Auto-DM a link to anyone who comments a keyword on an Instagram post
Self-host a free ManyChat-style comment-to-DM tool for creator clients
Track click-through rates on links sent via automated Instagram DMs

name: CopilotKit
description: The Frontend Stack for Agents & Generative UI. React, Angular, Mobile, Slack, and more.  Makers of the AG-UI Protocol
analysis: CopilotKit is a frontend SDK for building agent-native applications — chat UI, generative UI, shared state, and human-in-the-loop workflows — across React, Angular, Vue, React Native, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. It's for frontend/full-stack developers who already have an agent backend (LangGraph, CrewAI, PydanticAI, etc.) and need a UI layer that renders agent state and tool calls without a rewrite. Notable tech: the AG-UI protocol it created for agent-to-UI communication, a `useAgent` hook, and a large polyglot monorepo (TS/Python/C#/Java/Ruby).

use_cases.title: Add a chat/copilot UI to a React app backed by an AI agent
Render agent-generated UI components dynamically
Bring an existing LangGraph or CrewAI agent into Slack/Teams
Add human-approval steps to an agent workflow's frontend

name: watermarks-remover
description: Strip multi-vendor AI provenance marks: Unicode text hygiene, statistical rewrite hooks, and C2PA/metadata from PNG/JPEG/SVG/PDF/DOCX/HTML/MD
analysis: watermarks-remover is an agent skill paired with a stdlib-only Python HTTP service that strips multi-vendor AI provenance marks — invisible Unicode artifacts, statistical text watermarks (SynthID-text, Kirchenbauer-style), and C2PA/EXIF/XMP metadata — from text and files (PNG, JPEG, SVG, PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, and more). It ships as a thin agent skill (Claude, Cursor, Grok) that calls a local HTTP service over `/inspect`, `/detect`, and `/clean` endpoints, with Docker images bundling optional heavier detection backends (MarkLLM, MarkDiffusion, SynthID scorer). It's aimed at developers and privacy-conscious users who want to audit and clean AI-generation provenance markers from content they own, with explicit responsible-use documentation and fail-soft detection.

use_cases.title: Strip C2PA and EXIF provenance metadata from an AI-generated image
Detect and remove invisible Unicode watermarks from AI-written text
Run a local HTTP service to audit files for AI generation markers before publishing

name: Resource2Skill
description: A general framework for distilling human-created multimodal resources into reusable, executable skills that AI agents can browse, compose, and run, validated across diverse domains including web, PowerPoint, Excel, Blender, CAD, Unreal Engine 5, and REAPER-based music production.
analysis: Resource2Skill is a Microsoft Research framework and runtime that distills human-created multimodal resources (tutorial videos, articles, reference artifacts, code) into reusable, executable "skills" that an AI agent can browse, retrieve, compose, and run against real software tools. It ships domain adapters and MCP servers for Web (Playwright), PowerPoint, Excel, Blender, CAD, Unreal Engine 5, and REAPER-based music production, plus a skill-wiki/retrieval layer (BM25 + LLM rerank) and a CLI (`cli.py agent --domain ...`) for running tasks against a chosen domain. It's aimed at AI researchers and agent builders exploring skill-grounded agent execution rather than end users, and its distilled skill libraries are separately published as a Hugging Face dataset, backed by an accompanying arXiv paper.

use_cases.title: Distill a tutorial video into an executable skill an agent can reuse
Have an agent build a PowerPoint deck or Excel workbook via retrieved reference skills
Ground an agent's Blender or Unreal Engine actions in real prior examples
Browse and search a skill wiki with BM25 + LLM reranking before agent execution

name: kimi-k3-in-c
description: A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running inference on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM. Portable C99: no BLAS, no framework, no GPU.
analysis: kimi-k3-in-c is a from-scratch, dependency-free C99 inference engine that runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 mixture-of-experts model on a single CPU using only 8.24 GB of peak RAM, by streaming the 1.56 TB checkpoint's routed experts from disk (never resident) while keeping a small dense trunk in memory with an LRU expert cache. It uses AVX2/FMA SIMD kernels, MXFP4 quantization, and techniques like KDA linear attention and MLA to make an enormous MoE model runnable on ordinary consumer hardware (laptop to workstation) with byte-identical output regardless of RAM budget, only trading off speed. Aimed at systems programmers and ML engineers interested in low-level, zero-framework LLM inference engineering; extensively documented with benchmarks, architecture diagrams, and a test-gated build (make test) that validates against a PyTorch reference.

use_cases.title: Run a 2.78T-parameter model locally on a laptop with just 8GB RAM
Study a from-scratch C99 transformer/MoE inference engine implementation
Learn how expert streaming and LRU caching make huge MoE models fit in limited memory

name: kestra
description: Event Driven Orchestration & Scheduling Platform for Mission Critical Applications
analysis: Kestra is an open-source, event-driven orchestration platform for data, AI, and infrastructure workflows, defined declaratively in YAML and editable/visualizable from a built-in UI backed by a Java/Vue codebase. It supports both scheduled and real-time event triggers, hundreds of plugins (databases, cloud storage, Kafka, Spark, Slack, etc.), and scripting in any language, with Docker/Kubernetes/Helm deployment options to scale to millions of workflows. Targets data and platform engineers who want an infrastructure-as-code orchestrator with a friendlier UI than typical Airflow-style tools.

use_cases.title: Self-host an orchestration platform for scheduled and event-driven pipelines
Build data or ETL pipelines declaratively in YAML
Trigger workflows from real-time events like Kafka or file arrival

name: AiSOC
description: Open-source AI-powered Security Operations Center — alert fusion, purple-team drills, agent-assisted triage, MITRE ATT&CK investigation. MIT-licensed, self-hostable.
analysis: AiSOC is an open-source, self-hostable AI Security Operations Center that ingests security events from EDR/SIEM/cloud/identity/network sources, correlates and fuses alerts, and runs an AI agent (a ~600-line LangGraph orchestrator) to investigate incidents with a fully logged, replayable decision trail. It targets security teams who want an auditable, self-hosted alternative to closed-source AI SOC vendors, with detection content (Sigma/YARA/KQL rules), a public CI-gated eval harness, and deployment via Docker Compose, Helm, or Terraform. Built on Python/Go/TypeScript with Kafka, ClickHouse, Neo4j, and Postgres in its stack.

use_cases.title: Stand up a self-hosted AI-driven SOC console
Automate alert triage and noise suppression
Audit an AI agent's investigation reasoning step by step
Run purple-team drills against seeded incident scenarios

name: uniface
description: UniFace: A Unified Face Analysis Library for Python | Detection, alignment, landmarks, face-mesh, recognition, parsing, gaze, attributes and anti-spoofing under one API.
analysis: UniFace is a Python computer-vision library that unifies fifteen face-analysis tasks — detection, recognition/verification, tracking, landmarks, face mesh, parsing/segmentation, portrait matting, gaze/head-pose estimation, demographics, emotion, face states, quality assessment, anti-spoofing, and anonymization — behind one `FaceAnalyzer` API, backed by ONNX Runtime models (RetinaFace, ArcFace, BiSeNet, MODNet, etc.) that run on CPU, Apple Silicon, or CUDA. It ships a FAISS-backed embedding store and downloads SHA-256-verified weights on first use. This is a classical deep-learning face-analysis toolkit rather than an LLM or generative-media tool, so it doesn't fit the listed domains cleanly; it's filed under media-generation as the closest match.

use_cases.title: Detect and recognize faces in an image with one unified API
Anonymize faces in a dataset before publishing images
Check for spoofed or replayed faces in a liveness check
Estimate age, emotion, or gaze direction from a photo

name: technical
description: Various indicators developed or collected for the Freqtrade
analysis: Technical is a Python companion library for the Freqtrade crypto trading bot, providing a large collection of technical-analysis indicators (consensus models, VFI, Madrid ribbons, Ichimoku, trendlines, Fibonacci retracements, pivot points, Supertrend, ALMA, and more) plus dataframe utilities for timeframe resampling and merging. It wraps and standardizes indicators from around the community into a single pandas-dataframe-based API for use in Freqtrade strategy development. Aimed at algorithmic/crypto traders building custom strategies; mature and still actively maintained.

use_cases.title: Add technical indicators to a Freqtrade trading strategy
Resample and merge multi-timeframe OHLCV dataframes
Build a consensus signal across multiple indicators

name: freqtrade-strategies
description: Free trading strategies for Freqtrade bot
analysis: A community-contributed collection of free buy/sell strategy scripts for the Freqtrade cryptocurrency trading bot, covering technical-indicator strategies, futures variants, and lookahead-bias examples. It's explicitly meant as starting points to copy into a Freqtrade user_data/strategies folder and backtest/optimize yourself, not ready-to-run production strategies. Pure Python, no ML/LLM involved; long-running repo since 2018 that still receives contributions.

use_cases.title: Backtest a starter trading strategy before writing your own
Study example Freqtrade strategy implementations

name: frequi
description: Freqtrade UI - Frontend for Freqtrade
analysis: FreqUI is the official web dashboard for Freqtrade, an open-source crypto trading bot, built with Vue.js and PrimeVue. It lets traders monitor live/dry-run bots, view candlestick charts with indicator overlays, run and inspect backtests, and manage pairlists and settings through a browser instead of the CLI. It requires a running Freqtrade instance with its REST API enabled and is distributed both as a standalone Docker image and bundled inside Freqtrade itself.

use_cases.title: Monitor a live Freqtrade crypto trading bot from a web dashboard
Visualize backtest results and candlestick charts with indicators
Self-host a standalone UI in front of a Freqtrade REST API

name: freqtrade
description: Free, open source crypto trading bot
analysis: Freqtrade is a mature, free open-source Python crypto trading bot that automates buy/sell strategies across major exchanges (Binance, Kraken, Bybit, OKX, and more), with backtesting, hyperparameter optimization, machine-learning-driven strategy tuning (FreqAI), a built-in web UI, and Telegram remote control. It targets developers and traders comfortable writing Python strategy code who are expected to run in dry-run mode before risking real funds. An extremely active, long-running project (since 2017) with a strong community, CI pipeline, and Docker-based deployment.

use_cases.title: Automate a crypto trading strategy across multiple exchanges
Backtest and optimize a trading strategy with FreqAI
Control a running trading bot remotely via Telegram

name: the_well
description: A 15TB Collection of Physics Simulation Datasets
analysis: The Well is a 15TB collection of 16 numerical physics-simulation datasets (fluid dynamics, magnetohydrodynamics, acoustic scattering, biological systems, supernova/neutron-star mergers, etc.) packaged as a PyTorch-loadable Python library, plus benchmark surrogate-model training code (FNO and others) with Hydra-configured experiments and pretrained checkpoints on Hugging Face. It's aimed at ML researchers building physics-informed / PDE surrogate models who need large, diverse, standardized simulation data with a common dataset interface (WellDataset), streamable directly from Hugging Face or downloaded locally. Produced by Polymathic AI in collaboration with several universities and national labs, published at NeurIPS 2024.

use_cases.title: Train a PDE surrogate model on standardized physics data
Stream large physics simulation datasets from Hugging Face
Benchmark a new architecture against FNO baselines
Load fluid-dynamics or MHD simulation data into a training pipeline

name: AionUi
description: Open-source 24/7 Cowork app for OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and 20+ more CLI Agent | Customize your assistants | Team them up｜Star if you like it!
analysis: AionUi is a free, open-source desktop/web 'Cowork' application that lets a user run and orchestrate many CLI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw, Hermes, etc.) side by side with a built-in agent engine, multi-agent Team Mode, remote access via Telegram/Lark/WeChat, and 24/7 scheduled automation. It targets developers and power users who want one unified UI over dozens of AI agents plus office-document assistants (PPT/Word/Excel via OfficeCLI). Built on Electron/TypeScript with MCP tool management and ACP-based agent coordination.

use_cases.title: Run multiple CLI coding agents in one unified desktop UI
Set up a Leader/Teammate agent team to parallelize a task
Control coding agents remotely from a phone via Telegram or WeChat
Schedule unattended 24/7 agent automation with cron

name: agentswarms
description: Unified Agentic AI and Business Intelligence Platform
analysis: AgentSwarms is a self-hosted agentic AI plus business-intelligence platform combining a visual multi-agent workflow canvas, RAG knowledge bases, a semantic metric layer, data-warehouse connectors (Snowflake, BigQuery, Postgres, and more), and Python notebook developer workspaces. It generates BI dashboards, editable documents (PPTX/DOCX/XLSX), and SQL-grounded chat answers, enforcing per-user model rules, spend budgets, and a hash-chained audit trail before calls run, all deployed via Supabase and Docker with the user's own model provider keys. Aimed at teams and technical tinkerers who want an owned alternative to hosted agent-plus-BI platforms; built on TanStack Start, React, LangChain, and LangGraph.

use_cases.title: Stand up a self-hosted agentic BI platform with your own data
Design multi-agent swarm workflows on a visual canvas
Ground LLM answers in warehouse data with a semantic layer
Generate PowerPoint or Excel reports directly from agent chat

name: ntfy
description: Send push notifications to your phone or desktop using PUT/POST
analysis: ntfy is a mature, widely-used HTTP-based pub-sub push notification service written in Go that lets anyone send notifications to a phone or desktop via a simple PUT/POST request, with no signup required and official Android/iOS apps. It is self-hostable (the server and client are open source) with a hosted ntfy.sh offering paid tiers, and it targets developers and self-hosters wanting simple scriptable alerts, making it a common homelab, CI, and monitoring companion. Long track record since 2021, large community (Discord/Matrix), extensive documentation, and active ongoing maintenance.

use_cases.title: Send a notification to your phone from a shell script or cron job
Self-host a notification server for homelab alerts
Wire CI/CD or monitoring alerts into a simple HTTP endpoint

name: skill-recorder
description: Desktop app that records your on-screen work session and uses the GitHub Copilot CLI to reconstruct it as an intent + ordered steps, then builds a reusable Skill or Automation for Microsoft Scout, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, or Copilot Studio.
analysis: Skill Recorder is a Microsoft Electron desktop app (macOS primary, Windows supported) that records a user's on-screen work session — clicks, window/app switches, browser URLs, clipboard, and optional spoken narration — then uses the GitHub Copilot CLI to reconstruct the session into a clear intent plus ordered steps. From that reconstruction it generates a reusable `SKILL.md` Skill or a scheduled Automation for Microsoft Scout, Copilot Cowork, or Copilot Studio, preferring native agent tools (like `gh` CLI or web_fetch) over UI-click replay so a single recorded example generalizes to similar tasks. Aimed at non-technical and technical users who want to teach an AI agent a repeatable procedure by demonstrating it once, with local-only capture and explicit warnings about not recording secrets since Analyze sends data to GitHub's cloud.

use_cases.title: Record a manual workflow once and turn it into a reusable agent Skill
Generate a scheduled Automation from a demonstrated task
Teach an agent to fill out forms by demonstrating one example

name: context-ontology-accelerator
description: An open-source, ontology-based semantic context accelerator that enables AI agents to make more accurate, consistent, and explainable decisions.
analysis: An AWS open-source platform that builds a semantic context layer for AI agents by combining knowledge graphs, formal ontologies, and rule-based reasoning over enterprise data sources. It follows a Scan -> Model -> Serve architecture: ingesting and enriching data sources, inducing ontologies and metrics, then serving context to agents via a Virtual Knowledge Graph (SPARQL federation) and an MCP server, with namespace/role-based access control.
