Migration importer. Recurring autonomous tasks.
analysis: Skales is a closed-source, cross-platform (Windows/macOS/Linux/Android/iOS) personal AI desktop agent with a free built-in trial or BYOK across 15+ providers, offline Ollama support, and features spanning chat, a coding mode with inline diffs, an image/video/design studio, desktop automation, and agent-to-agent pairing between devices. This GitHub repo is only the distribution/release channel (changelog, installers, issue tracker) plus a stale historical v7 source snapshot under a source-available BSL 1.1 license; the actual shipped app is closed source and not built from this repo. Aimed at non-technical end users wanting a local, low-friction AI agent rather than developers wanting to build from source.

use_cases.title: Install a no-terminal local AI agent for everyday tasks
Bind a folder to chat for AI-assisted coding with diffs
Pair a phone to control a desktop agent remotely

name: kong
description: The world's first agentic reverse engineer.
analysis: Kong is an agentic reverse-engineering CLI that automates binary analysis: it drives Ghidra in-process (via PyGhidra) to triage, LLM-decompile, deobfuscate, and rename functions/structs in stripped or obfuscated binaries, then writes recovered names and types back into Ghidra's program database. Aimed at security researchers and reverse engineers, it supports Claude and OpenAI as LLM backends, includes an agentic deobfuscation pipeline for anti-RE techniques (control-flow flattening, VM protection, string encryption), and ships an eval harness scoring output against ground-truth source.

use_cases.title: Auto-recover function names and types from a stripped binary
Deobfuscate a binary with control-flow flattening or VM protection
Run an LLM-guided decompilation pipeline over an unknown binary
Score reverse-engineering output accuracy against known source

name: GLM-OCR
description: GLM-OCR: Accurate ×  Fast × Comprehensive
analysis: GLM-OCR is a compact (0.9B parameter) multimodal OCR model from Zhipu AI for complex document understanding — layout analysis, table/formula recognition, and information extraction — built on a GLM-V encoder-decoder with a CogViT visual encoder. It targets developers building document-parsing pipelines who need either a hosted MaaS API or self-hosted deployment via vLLM, SGLang, or Ollama, and ships a Python SDK/CLI (`glmocr`), a Flask service mode, and a React frontend/FastAPI backend demo app. It claims #1 on the OmniDocBench V1.5 benchmark.

use_cases.title: Extract markdown/JSON from scanned PDFs and images
Self-host an OCR model behind vLLM or SGLang
Parse complex tables and formulas from business documents

name: agents-course
description: This repository contains the Hugging Face Agents Course.
analysis: The Hugging Face Agents Course is a free, structured curriculum teaching how to build AI agents, delivered as MDX lesson content plus quizzes and a small companion Python quiz-pusher script. It covers agent fundamentals, then hands-on units on smolagents, LlamaIndex, and LangGraph, agentic RAG, fine-tuning for function-calling, observability/evaluation, and a final certified project with a leaderboard. It targets developers and students learning agent frameworks from Hugging Face, with translations maintained by the community.

use_cases.title: Learn how AI agents and LLM tool-calling work from scratch
Compare smolagents, LangGraph, and LlamaIndex agent frameworks
Follow a hands-on unit on fine-tuning an LLM for function calling
Build an agentic RAG use case and get it certified via the final project

name: context-hub
analysis: Context Hub (chub) is a CLI and MCP server that gives coding agents curated, versioned, language-specific API documentation instead of letting them guess or scrape the web. Agents run `chub search`/`chub get` to fetch docs, can attach local annotations when they find gaps, and can send up/down feedback back to maintainers to improve the shared content over time. It's built for agent builders on tools like Claude Code and Cursor who want more reliable code generation against real APIs, with all doc content stored as open markdown in the repo.

use_cases.title: Fetch curated API docs for a coding agent mid-task
Wire chub into Claude Code as an agent skill
Let agents leave annotations that persist across sessions

name: agency-agents
description: A complete AI agency at your fingertips - From frontend wizards to Reddit community ninjas, from whimsy injectors to reality checkers. Each agent is a specialized expert with personality, processes, and proven deliverables.
analysis: Agency Agents is a large library of markdown-defined AI agent personas (engineering, design, academic, finance, game-dev, and more) meant to be installed into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and other coding assistants. Each agent file encodes an identity, workflows, and deliverables so a generic coding assistant can be switched into a specialized persona on demand. Install scripts and a companion native app handle cross-tool installation and updates. Aimed at solo developers who want ready-made specialist subagents without writing their own system prompts.

use_cases.title: Install specialized coding subagents into Claude Code
Add domain-expert agent personas to Cursor or Codex
Browse agent definitions for prompt-engineering ideas
Install only specific agent divisions like engineering or security

name: autoresearch
description: AI agents running research on single-GPU nanochat training automatically
analysis: Autoresearch, from Andrej Karpathy, is a minimal single-GPU LLM training harness designed to be driven autonomously by a coding agent (Claude/Codex) overnight: the agent edits train.py (a simplified nanochat GPT implementation with Muon+AdamW optimizer), runs fixed 5-minute training experiments, checks the val_bpb metric, and keeps or discards changes in a loop guided by a program.md instruction file. It's aimed at ML researchers and hobbyists experimenting with agent-driven neural architecture/hyperparameter search on a single NVIDIA GPU (tested on H100). The repo is intentionally tiny (three files) and had a short burst of activity in March 2026 with community forks adding macOS/Windows/AMD support.

use_cases.title: Let a coding agent autonomously iterate on a small GPT training loop overnight
Study a minimal single-GPU nanochat-style training implementation
Prototype agent-driven hyperparameter/architecture search on limited compute

name: llm-whatgives
description: Hundreds of models & providers. One command to find what runs on your hardware.
analysis: llmfit (repo name llm-whatgives, upstream AlexsJones/llmfit) is a Rust terminal tool that detects a machine's RAM, CPU, and GPU/VRAM, then scores hundreds of LLM models across fit, speed, quality, and context to recommend which will actually run well on that hardware. It ships an interactive TUI plus a classic CLI/JSON mode for scripting, supports multi-GPU and MoE architectures, dynamic quantization selection, and integrates with local runtime providers (Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX, Docker Model Runner, LM Studio), with a community benchmark-sharing system for real tok/s numbers. It targets developers and self-hosters deciding which local LLM to download and run on their specific hardware.

use_cases.title: Find which local LLMs will run well on your specific GPU/CPU/RAM
Get a JSON-formatted model recommendation for a script or agent
Benchmark real tok/s on your machine and compare to community results
Pick a quantization and runtime provider (Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX) for a given model

name: learn-claude-code
description: Bash is all you need -  A nano claude code–like 「agent harness」, built from 0 to 1
analysis: A structured, multi-language (English/Chinese/Japanese) tutorial series that teaches how to build an agent harness from scratch, mirroring Claude Code's architecture: the agent loop, tool use, permissions, hooks, todo tracking, subagents, context compaction, task systems, and worktree isolation, each as a runnable Python lesson with an accompanying README and diagrams. It's aimed at engineers who want to understand agent-harness engineering, as distinct from prompt-chaining frameworks, by building the mechanisms themselves rather than reading about them abstractly. An extremely popular educational repo (74k+ stars) with a companion learn.shareai.run site.

use_cases.title: Learn how Claude Code's agent loop actually works
Build a minimal coding-agent harness step by step
Study subagent and worktree isolation patterns
Teach a team the mechanics behind agent tooling

name: agent-openai-python-banking-assistant
description: Multi-agent banking assistant with Python and Microsoft Agent Framework
analysis: An Azure Samples reference architecture for a multi-agent banking assistant built on Python and the Microsoft Agent Framework, with a React chat widget and Java/business-API microservices. It demonstrates supervisor-based orchestration where domain agents (account, transaction, payment) hand off tasks, expose business logic to agents via MCP tools, and use Azure Document Intelligence for invoice OCR. Intended as a starting template for teams building conversational, multi-agent business assistants on Azure Container Apps with Azure OpenAI/Foundry.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a multi-agent business assistant on Azure
Learn supervisor/hand-off orchestration patterns with Microsoft Agent Framework
Wire existing business REST APIs to agents via MCP
Add OCR-driven invoice payment flows with Document Intelligence

name: python-agentframework-demos
analysis: This is Microsoft's official sample collection demonstrating the Python Microsoft Agent Framework, covering agent basics, tool calling, multi-turn sessions, persistent history (SQLite/Redis), long-term memory (Redis, Mem0), sub-agent context isolation, tool-approval gating, middleware, RAG knowledge retrieval (Azure AI Search, Postgres pgvector, SQLite FTS5), MCP server integration (local and remote), and multi-agent workflows (fan-out/fan-in, sequential orchestration, MagenticOne, streaming). It supports Microsoft Foundry (Azure OpenAI), OpenAI.com, and local Ollama models, and includes IaC (Bicep) for provisioning Azure resources plus a devcontainer/Codespaces setup. Aimed at Python developers learning or evaluating the Microsoft Agent Framework for building production-grade agentic applications.

use_cases.title: Learn Microsoft Agent Framework patterns like tool calling, memory, and RAG
Build a multi-agent workflow with fan-out/fan-in or sequential orchestration
Connect an agent to a local or remote MCP server for tool use
Provision Azure OpenAI models via Bicep IaC for agent experiments

name: system-prompts-and-models-of-ai-tools
description: FULL Augment Code, Claude Code, Cluely, CodeBuddy, Comet, Cursor, Devin AI, Junie, Kiro, Leap.new, Lovable, Manus, NotionAI, Orchids.app, Perplexity, Poke, Qoder, Replit, Same.dev, Trae, Traycer AI, VSCode Agent, Warp.dev, Windsurf, Xcode, Z.ai Code, Dia & v0. (And other Open Sourced) System Prompts, Internal Tools & AI Models
analysis: A massive, frequently-updated collection of leaked and extracted system prompts, tool definitions, and internal configs from dozens of commercial AI coding and assistant tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Devin, Windsurf, v0, Replit, Lovable, Manus, and many more). It is a pure reference archive of .txt/.json files with no code, used by prompt engineers and AI researchers to study how production AI products structure their system prompts and tool schemas. Extremely popular (142k+ stars) and actively growing with new tool prompts added regularly.

use_cases.title: Study how production AI coding tools structure system prompts
Compare tool-call schemas across different AI coding agents
Find inspiration for writing your own agent's system prompt

name: dify
description: Build Agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, with rich AI model and tool support on one collaborative workspace. Deploy on cloud, VPC, or self-hosted, so teams move from prototype to production without rebuilding the stack.
analysis: Dify is a widely-adopted open-source LLM application development platform combining a visual workflow builder, RAG pipeline, agent tooling (function calling / ReAct with 50+ built-in tools), a prompt IDE, and LLMOps observability into one self-hostable or cloud-hosted product. It supports hundreds of model providers and exposes every feature as an API, so teams can go from prototype chatbots/agents to production backend services without writing glue code. Deployed via Docker Compose, Kubernetes, or major cloud Terraform/CDK modules; has an enterprise edition.

use_cases.title: Build a RAG-based chatbot without writing backend code
Design agentic workflows on a visual canvas
Self-host an LLM app platform for a team

name: claude-quickstarts
description: A collection of projects designed to help developers quickly get started with building deployable applications using the Claude API
analysis: Anthropic's official collection of starter projects for building on the Claude API, including a customer support agent, financial data analyst, computer-use and browser-use demos, an autonomous coding agent built on the Claude Agent SDK, and several Managed Agents examples (chat SDK, CopilotKit/AG-UI, knowledge wiki). Each subproject is a self-contained, cloneable reference implementation with its own README and setup steps, meant for developers learning Claude API patterns like tool use, computer use, and multi-agent orchestration. Mixed Python/TypeScript stack with Docker support for the computer/browser-use demos.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a Claude-powered customer support agent
Give Claude control of a desktop or browser
Build an autonomous multi-session coding agent
Wire a Managed Agents session into a chat UI

name: agentfield
description: Build, run and scale AI agents like API and microservices
analysis: AgentField is an open-source control plane that turns agent functions written in Python, Go, or TypeScript into production REST APIs, handling routing, fan-out, retries, async execution, human-in-the-loop pauses, and observability across thousands of concurrent agent invocations. It targets developers building multi-agent backends who want their existing framework code (LangGraph, CrewAI, etc.) to run as durable, callable microservices rather than one-off scripts. Notable tech includes a Go control plane, SDKs in three languages, Kubernetes/Docker deployment, and a coding-agent installer flow (works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI).

use_cases.title: Turn agent functions into production REST endpoints
Fan out one request across thousands of parallel agent branches
Add human approval gates to autonomous agent workflows
Deploy a multi-agent backend with Docker Compose or Kubernetes

name: clawtime
description: An engaging 1-on-1 chat interface between you and your AI agent.
analysis: ClawTime is a self-hosted Node.js web chat interface that connects directly over WebSocket to a locally running OpenClaw AI agent gateway, offering voice conversations (browser speech recognition plus edge-tts), an animated 3D voxel avatar reflecting agent state, passkey (WebAuthn) authentication, and end-to-end encryption. It stores all history and credentials locally (`~/.clawtime/`) rather than routing through cloud chat services, and is designed to be installed and customized by the AI agent itself via a bundled SKILL.md. It targets hobbyists running a personal OpenClaw agent who want a private, expressive chat UI instead of a generic cloud chatbot.

use_cases.title: Give a self-hosted AI agent a private voice-and-avatar chat UI
Talk to a local AI agent by voice from a mobile browser over a tunnel
Let an agent customize its own chat interface and avatar in real time

name: SQL-AI-samples
description: Samples using AI and Azure SQL DB
analysis: SQL-AI-samples is Microsoft's official collection of sample notebooks, scripts, and end-to-end projects showing how to build AI applications on Azure SQL Database, covering vector embeddings and similarity search (Cognitive Search, FAISS, Redis/ACRE, custom IVFFlat/KMeans indexes), RAG chatbots (LangChain, Semantic Kernel, PromptFlow), NL2SQL agents, content moderation, and an MSSQL MCP server for agent tool access. It's organized as a grab-bag reference repo of Jupyter notebooks and small standalone projects (many linking out to sibling Azure-Samples repos) rather than a single cohesive product, aimed at developers integrating Azure OpenAI/AI Search with SQL-backed data. It's steadily maintained with periodic additions rather than fast-moving, reflecting its role as a documentation/sample companion to Azure SQL AI features.

use_cases.title: Learn how to generate and query vector embeddings directly from Azure SQL Database
Build a NL2SQL chatbot over your own Azure SQL data with LangChain
Connect an AI agent to an MSSQL database via the official MCP server
Compare FAISS, Redis, and native SQL vector indexing approaches on the same dataset

name: sql-ai-datathon
analysis: A Microsoft-run hackathon starter repo with four guided missions teaching how to build AI-powered applications on SQL Server 2025/Azure SQL: embeddings and vector search, RAG chat over SQL data, orchestrating SQL+AI workflows in C#/Python, and a full-stack AI app, culminating in an open-ended hack submission for SQLCon 2026. It's a devcontainer-based, fork-and-clone workshop template for developers learning vector search and RAG patterns specifically on Microsoft SQL, not a general-purpose library or ongoing product. Time-boxed event repo with low traffic outside the datathon window.

use_cases.title: Learn vector search and RAG on SQL Server via guided missions
Fork a datathon starter for a SQL+AI hackathon
Build a chatbot grounded in SQL Server data
Prototype a full-stack AI app with Data API Builder

name: Auto-Claude
description: Autonomous multi-session AI coding
analysis: Aperant (formerly Auto-Claude) is a cross-platform Electron desktop app that orchestrates autonomous multi-agent coding sessions on top of Claude Code, running up to 12 parallel agent terminals in isolated git worktrees with a kanban-style task board. It handles planning, implementation, self-validating QA, and AI-assisted merge-conflict resolution, and integrates with GitHub/GitLab and Linear. Targeted at developers who want hands-off, parallelized autonomous coding backed by a Claude subscription; the 2.x app is currently in maintenance mode while a 3.0 rewrite happens in a separate repo.

use_cases.title: Run multiple autonomous coding agents in parallel worktrees
Turn a GitHub issue into an AI-implemented pull request
Track agent coding tasks on a kanban board

name: aithing
description: AI, Agents, and Automation
analysis: AI Thing is a privacy-first, BYOK desktop AI automation app for macOS (Swift/AppKit) with a companion Tauri-based cross-platform shell, letting users run frontier models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) and connect agents like Google Workspace, GitHub, and Notion via MCP servers. It supports background automations, multi-model switching within a single conversation, and complex multi-app tasks, all with local storage of conversations and API keys instead of a hosted backend. It targets individuals who want a self-hosted alternative to paid agent platforms and is now fully open source. Notable tech: Swift/SwiftUI native macOS app, Firebase auth, Tauri/Rust shell, MCP client integration.

use_cases.title: Run background AI automations that span multiple apps and tools
Use your own Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini API keys in a local-first chat client
Connect an AI agent to GitHub, Google Workspace, and Notion via MCP
Switch between multiple frontier models mid-conversation on desktop

name: claude-code-agentic-rag-masterclass
description: Build an agentic RAG app from scratch by collaborating with Claude Code. 8-module course covering hybrid search, reranking, text-to-SQL, subagents, and more. React + FastAPI + Supabase.
analysis: This is a companion repo and starter scaffold for an 8-module video course that teaches building an agentic RAG application from scratch by pair-programming with Claude Code. It covers chunking, hybrid search, reranking, text-to-SQL, and subagent patterns on a React + FastAPI + Supabase (pgvector) stack, and ships with a PRD, progress tracker, and Claude Code slash commands (/onboard, /build) rather than a finished app. Aimed at non-coders or junior builders who want a guided, AI-assisted path to a production-style RAG system.

use_cases.title: Follow a guided course to build an agentic RAG app by directing Claude Code
Learn hybrid search, reranking, and text-to-SQL patterns for a RAG pipeline
Use as a starter template with Claude Code slash commands for a Supabase-backed RAG app

name: worldmonitor
description: Real-time global intelligence dashboard. AI-powered news aggregation, geopolitical monitoring, and infrastructure tracking in a unified situational awareness interface
analysis: World Monitor is a real-time, AI-powered global-intelligence dashboard that aggregates news, geopolitical, financial, and infrastructure signals (with a Country Instability Index, dual 3D/flat map engines, flight data, and cross-stream correlation) into a single situational-awareness interface. It ships as public web variants (world/tech/finance/commodity/happy/energy), a Tauri desktop app for macOS/Windows/Linux, an MCP server plus REST API, and official CLI/SDKs (npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Go), supporting local-only inference via Ollama for privacy-conscious users.

use_cases.title: Monitor global geopolitical and infrastructure risk on one dashboard
Query world-event and risk data programmatically via MCP or REST
Run the dashboard locally with Ollama for offline, private AI synthesis
Track a country's instability index over time via the CLI or SDK

name: get-shit-done
description: A light-weight and powerful meta-prompting, context engineering and spec-driven development system for Claude Code by TÂCHES.
analysis: GSD was a lightweight meta-prompting, context-engineering and spec-driven-development system for Claude Code, providing structured phase/plan/milestone workflows via slash commands and hooks. The repository is now archived and its README simply redirects users to the successor project 'GSD Core' at open-gsd/gsd-core, where active development continues. Kept only as a historical pointer; not usable or maintained in its current form.

use_cases.title: Find the successor project for archived GSD tooling
Reference historical spec-driven-development workflow design for Claude Code

name: opendocmgmnt
description: Lightweight document management system packed with all the features you can expect from big expensive solutions
analysis: Teedy (formerly sismics/docs) is a lightweight, self-hostable document management system with OCR, full-text search, tagging, workflow, versioning, AES-256 encryption, 2FA, and a REST API, plus a native Android client. It targets individuals and small businesses wanting DMS features (comparable to expensive commercial solutions) without the cost, deployable via Docker/Java. Long-running (since 2013), actively maintained with a Docker image, PostgreSQL support, and a live demo.

use_cases.title: Self-host a document management system with OCR search
Set up team file sharing with permissions and audit logs
Replace an expensive enterprise DMS with an open-source one

name: 302_video_generator
description: 🎬🤖 302 AI Video Generator! 🚀✨
analysis: A Next.js web app that wraps the 302.AI video generation API, letting users create AI videos from text and images through models like Luma, Runway Gen-3, Kling, and CogVideoX. It is the open-source frontend for the closed-source 302.AI service and requires a 302.AI API key to function, rather than running any model locally. Built with Next.js 14, Tailwind/Shadcn UI, Zod/react-hook-form, and Zustand, and ships as a Docker image for self-hosting. Development appears to have stalled after August 2025 with no recent commits.

use_cases.title: Self-host a multi-provider AI video generation UI
Prototype a branded AI video tool on top of 302.AI's API
Compare Luma, Runway, Kling and CogVideoX outputs from one interface

name: dexter
description: An autonomous agent for deep financial research
analysis: Dexter is an autonomous financial research agent built in TypeScript/Bun that decomposes complex financial questions into research plans, autonomously calls tools to pull real-time market data (income statements, balance sheets, cash flow), self-checks its work, and iterates until confident. It ships as an interactive terminal UI (like Claude Code but for finance), includes an eval suite with LangSmith tracking and LLM-as-judge scoring, a scratchpad debug log, and a WhatsApp gateway so users can chat with the agent via their own WhatsApp number. It is explicitly for educational/informational use, not real trading advice, and targets developers or hobbyists exploring agentic financial research.

use_cases.title: Ask an autonomous agent to research a stock using live financial statements
Chat with a financial research agent through your own WhatsApp number
Evaluate agent accuracy on financial Q&A with LLM-as-judge scoring
Study a real-world TUI agent architecture for task planning and tool execution

name: audioghost-ai
description: Extract any sound with text prompts. Memory-optimized SAM-Audio with modern UI.
analysis: AudioGhost AI is a full-stack web app for text-prompted audio source separation: users describe a sound in natural language (e.g. "vocals", "a dog barking") and the app extracts or removes it from an uploaded audio or video file. It wraps Meta's SAM-Audio model in a memory-optimized "lite mode" that cuts VRAM usage up to 40%, with a Next.js/Tailwind frontend, FastAPI backend, and Celery/Redis task queue for async processing. Aimed at hobbyists and audio engineers with a CUDA GPU who want local, prompt-driven stem separation without a full 12GB+ VRAM requirement.

use_cases.title: Extract vocals or specific sounds from an audio file using a text prompt
Remove background noise or a specific sound source from a video's audio track
Run SAM-Audio inference locally on a consumer GPU with reduced VRAM footprint

name: crmtwenty
description: The open alternative to Salesforce, designed for AI.
analysis: Twenty is a large, well-funded open-source CRM (an alternative to Salesforce) built as a TypeScript monorepo with a NestJS/PostgreSQL/Redis backend and a React frontend, letting technical teams define custom objects, fields, and views as code and extend the CRM with a CLI-scaffolded app system. It ships AI agents and chat features built into the CRM itself, GraphQL APIs, workflow automation, and self-hosting via Docker Compose alongside a managed cloud offering. It's aimed at businesses and developers who want a CRM they can version, extend, and self-host rather than rent from a closed SaaS vendor, and is one of the most active and heavily starred open-source CRM projects.

use_cases.title: Self-host an open-source Salesforce alternative for a small business or startup
Scaffold a custom CRM app with defined objects, fields, and views as code
Give a sales team AI agents and chat built directly into their pipeline tool
Track deals, contacts, and companies in a version-controlled, developer-friendly CRM

name: claude-code-scheduler
description: Put Claude on autopilot
analysis: A Claude Code plugin that schedules one-time and recurring tasks (natural-language triggers like 'every weekday at 9am') and runs them headlessly via `claude -p`, registering with the OS's native scheduler (launchd, crontab, Task Scheduler). Supports autonomous execution with permission bypass, optional git-worktree isolation for changes, execution logging, and slash commands for managing schedules. Built for developers who want Claude Code to run recurring code reviews, audits, or maintenance tasks unattended.

use_cases.title: Schedule recurring Claude Code review or audit tasks
Run Claude Code autonomously overnight with worktree isolation
Automate dependency and dead-code checks on a cron schedule

name: pro-workflow
description: Claude Code learns from your corrections: self-correcting memory that compounds over 50+ sessions. Context engineering, parallel worktrees, agent teams, and 17 battle-tested skills.
analysis: Pro Workflow is a Claude Code plugin (also installable into 30+ agents via `skills add`) that layers a SQLite-backed self-correcting memory, FTS5-indexed research wikis, and quality-gate hooks on top of coding sessions, so corrections become durable rules and research persists across sessions. It ships 41 skills, 8 agents, 23 commands, and 37 hook scripts covering things like cost tracking, permission tuning, and a budget-capped auto-research loop with multi-LLM council deliberation. Aimed at heavy Claude Code / Cursor users who want cross-session memory and knowledge accumulation instead of losing context on every compaction.

use_cases.title: Give Claude Code persistent memory of corrections across sessions
Build a searchable research wiki inside a coding agent
Track token cost and permission denials for agent sessions

name: claude-code-best-practice
description: from vibe coding to agentic engineering - practice makes claude perfect
analysis: A very popular, near-daily-updated reference repo documenting the full Claude Code feature surface (subagents, commands, skills, hooks, MCP, workflows, agent teams, scheduled tasks, and more) with paired 'best practice' and 'implemented' example docs for each concept. It bundles a working example .claude/ config (agents, commands, skills, hooks with sound effects) that readers can copy directly, plus presentation decks and video transcripts. Aimed at Claude Code power users and teams wanting a living cheat-sheet of the tool's rapidly expanding capabilities.

use_cases.title: Learn how to structure Claude Code subagents and skills
Copy working .claude config examples into a new project
Keep up with new Claude Code features as they ship

name: Run-Local-LLMs-on-Any-Device
description: GPT4All: Run Local LLMs on Any Device. Open-source and available for commercial use.
analysis: This is a fork/mirror of Nomic AI's GPT4All, a desktop application (with Python and C++ bindings and a Qt UI) for running open-weight LLMs such as Llama 3 and Mistral locally via llama.cpp, requiring no GPU or API key, plus a "LocalDocs" RAG feature for chatting with local files. It targets non-technical users who want a private, offline chat application as well as Python developers wanting a simple local-inference client. This particular fork/mirror shows no push activity beyond its original snapshot and has only a handful of stars, indicating a stale copy rather than an actively maintained project (the actual upstream GPT4All repo is far larger and more active).

use_cases.title: Run an open-weight LLM chatbot fully offline on a laptop
Chat with local documents via LocalDocs RAG
Embed a local LLM in a Python app via the gpt4all client

name: mem0
description: Universal memory layer for AI Agents
analysis: Mem0 is a widely-adopted universal memory layer for AI agents and assistants, giving them persistent, personalized user/session/agent-level memory with multi-signal (semantic + BM25 + entity) retrieval and temporal reasoning. Offered as a Python/TypeScript library, a self-hosted Docker server, a managed cloud platform, and a CLI, plus installable Claude Code/Codex/Cursor 'skills' for wiring memory into a codebase. Backed by a published paper and a YC-backed company, used for chatbots, customer support, and long-term-memory agentic applications.

use_cases.title: Add persistent long-term memory to an LLM chatbot
Self-host a Mem0 memory server for a team of agents
Wire Mem0 into an existing repo via the mem0-integrate skill
Retrieve user preferences across sessions for personalized responses

name: Flowise
description: Build AI Agents, Visually
analysis: Flowise is a low-code/no-code visual builder for LLM applications and AI agents, letting users drag-and-drop nodes (LangChain components, agentflow steps, chatbots, RAG pipelines) into a workflow without writing code, then deploy it as a chatbot or API. It's a full-stack TypeScript monorepo (Node backend, React UI, third-party component integrations) that self-hosts via Docker or npm, with observability hooks for Prometheus/Grafana/OpenTelemetry. It's aimed at teams and builders who want a GUI over LangChain-style agent orchestration instead of hand-writing agent code. The project has been archived by its maintainers as of 2026, so it should be treated as a historical/frozen reference rather than an actively developed platform.

use_cases.title: Build a RAG chatbot visually without writing LangChain code
Self-host a drag-and-drop agent builder for a small team
Reference an archived visual-agent-builder architecture before migrating to an alternative
Expose a visually built agent flow as a callable API endpoint

name: claude-mem
description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent –  Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
analysis: Claude-Mem is a persistent memory system for coding agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Gemini, and more) that hooks into agent lifecycle events, compresses tool-use observations into semantic summaries via AI, stores them in SQLite plus a Chroma vector database, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. It's for developers who want continuity across agent sessions without manually re-explaining project context, installed via `npx claude-mem install` or the Claude Code plugin marketplace. It ships MCP search tools (search/timeline/get_observations), a local worker service with a web viewer, and optional cloud sync.

use_cases.title: Persist project context across Claude Code sessions
Search past agent observations with semantic queries
Add long-term memory to OpenCode, Codex, or Gemini CLI agents

name: ChatDev
description: ChatDev 2.0: Dev All through LLM-powered Multi-Agent Collaboration
analysis: ChatDev 2.0 (DevAll) is a zero-code multi-agent orchestration platform where users configure agents, workflows, and tasks through a web console to automate complex work such as data visualization, 3D generation, and deep research; the legacy ChatDev 1.0 (on a separate branch) simulated a virtual software company with CEO/CTO/Programmer agents automating the full SDLC. The backend is Python/uv with a Vue 3 + Vite frontend, Docker Compose deployment, and integration hooks for coding-agent tools that can invoke or create ChatDev workflows. Backed by OpenBMB with an associated NeurIPS paper on evolving multi-agent orchestration; a large, long-running research-to-product project with over 34,000 stars.

use_cases.title: Build a no-code multi-agent workflow for a custom task
Automate a research or content pipeline with agent teams
Study multi-agent software-development collaboration patterns

name: ai-data-science-team
description: An AI-powered data science team of agents to help you perform common data science tasks 10X faster.
analysis: AI Data Science Team is a Python library of specialized LLM agents (data cleaning, wrangling, visualization, feature engineering, SQL, EDA, H2O ML, MLflow) built on LangChain/LangGraph-style patterns, plus a flagship Streamlit app called AI Pipeline Studio for visual, reproducible data pipelines. It targets data scientists and ML engineers who want to automate common data-science grunt work using OpenAI or local Ollama models. The repo bundles runnable example apps (pandas analyst, SQL analyst, exploratory copilot) and notebooks demonstrating each agent.

use_cases.title: Automate data cleaning and wrangling with an LLM agent instead of writing pandas by hand
Build a visual, reproducible data pipeline with AI-assisted steps via AI Pipeline Studio
Ask natural-language questions over a SQL database using the SQL Database Agent
Generate exploratory data analysis reports automatically with the EDA Tools Agent

name: ten-framework
description: Open-source framework for conversational voice AI agents
analysis: TEN Framework is an open-source real-time multimodal conversational AI framework for building voice/video agents that combine ASR, LLM, and TTS extensions (STT/LLM/TTS pluggable via a visual TMAN Designer) with low-latency RTC and WebSocket transport. It ships ready-made agent examples (multi-purpose voice assistant, lip-sync avatars with Live2D/HeyGen/Tavus, speaker diarization, SIP phone calls, live transcription, ESP32 hardware integration) and a broader ecosystem including TEN VAD and TEN Turn Detection for full-duplex dialogue. Implemented across Python, C/C++, TypeScript, Rust and Go, deployable via Docker or Codespaces, and targeted at developers building production voice AI assistants, avatars, and telephony bots.

use_cases.title: Build a low-latency real-time voice assistant with pluggable STT/LLM/TTS
Create a lip-synced avatar agent using Live2D or HeyGen
Add phone call support to an AI agent via SIP
Run real-time speaker diarization for a multi-party voice application

name: copilot-camp
description: Hands-on labs for extending Microsoft 365 Copilot and building custom engine agents
analysis: Microsoft's official hands-on workshop repo for building and extending Microsoft 365 Copilot: declarative agents, custom-engine agents (M365 Agents SDK + Semantic Kernel, or Agent Framework), Copilot Cowork extensibility, MCP servers with Entra ID auth, and SharePoint agents. Structured as multiple bundled lab tracks (A-E) with full C#/TypeScript/Bicep sample projects (e.g. an insurance-claims agent with vision analysis and document search) for enterprise developers on the Microsoft stack.

use_cases.title: Follow guided labs to build a Microsoft 365 Copilot declarative agent
Build a custom-engine agent with the M365 Agents SDK and Semantic Kernel
Secure an MCP server with OAuth 2.0 and Entra ID
Ground a Copilot agent in enterprise data via Copilot Connectors

name: antigravity-awesome-skills
description: AAS Core is the local, agent-first control plane for complete catalog discovery, agent-owned selection, stack validation, and planning, backed by 2,005+ agentic skills. Includes CLI, local MCP, catalog, plugins, and Workbench.
analysis: AAS Core (agentic-awesome-skills) is a large local, agent-first catalog and control plane of 2,000+ reusable SKILL.md playbooks for coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Kiro, Copilot, and more), packaged as a local MCP server, CLI, and a browser-local Workbench for reviewing agent-selected skill stacks. Instead of ranking or auto-installing skills, it lets the agent inspect a project, search the full catalog, and compose a validated, reproducible manifest (aas-stack.json) before anything is applied. It targets developers who want a curated, distributable skill/plugin ecosystem across multiple AI coding agents rather than ad-hoc prompt copying.

use_cases.title: Install a curated skill pack for Claude Code or Cursor from a large catalog
Let an agent search and compose its own validated skill stack via local MCP
Review and approve an agent's proposed skill selection before applying it
Bootstrap a new coding agent project with a specialized plugin bundle

name: IPTV
description: M3U Playlist for free TV channels
analysis: This repository maintains a curated, community-sourced M3U8 playlist of free, legal-to-stream TV channels from around the world, organized by country in per-country markdown files and compiled into a single playlist via a Python script. It targets IPTV app users who want a ready-made channel list rather than software to build with, and enforces a strict quality bar (HD only, one URL per channel, no paid or geoblocked-only content). It is very actively maintained with automated CI to validate and rebuild the playlist.

use_cases.title: Point an IPTV player at a maintained free-TV playlist by country
Contribute a new free, legal streaming channel via pull request

name: PageIndex
description: 📑 PageIndex: Document Index for Vectorless, Reasoning-based RAG
analysis: PageIndex is a vectorless, reasoning-based RAG library that builds a hierarchical table-of-contents-style tree index from long PDF documents and lets an LLM navigate that tree via reasoning rather than vector similarity search, aiming for traceable, explainable retrieval on professional documents (financial reports, legal filings, regulatory text). It's for developers building document QA/agentic retrieval systems who are frustrated by chunking artifacts and opaque vector search, and it reports 98.7% accuracy on FinanceBench. The open-source Python package covers standard PDF parsing and tree generation, while enhanced OCR, hosted chat, and MCP/API access are offered as a cloud service.

use_cases.title: Build reasoning-based retrieval over long PDFs without a vector DB
Generate a table-of-contents tree index for a financial or legal document
Wire agentic vectorless RAG into an OpenAI Agents SDK pipeline

name: Stealth-Requests
description: Undetected web-scraping & seamless HTML parsing in Python!
analysis: Stealth-Requests is a Python HTTP library, API-compatible with `requests`, that uses curl_cffi to mimic Chrome's TLS/HTTP fingerprint for undetected web scraping, with automatic User-Agent rotation, Referer tracking, and built-in retry logic for 429/503/522 responses. Its response object adds convenience methods for extracting emails, phone numbers, images, links, and HTML tables, converting pages to Lxml/BeautifulSoup trees, and rendering HTML to Markdown, with both sync and asyncio session support. Aimed at developers building scrapers or data-extraction pipelines who want fewer blocks and less parsing boilerplate than raw `requests` + `bs4`.

use_cases.title: Scrape a site without triggering bot-detection fingerprinting
Extract emails, links, and tables from a page in one call
Convert a scraped webpage into clean Markdown for an LLM pipeline
Run concurrent async scraping sessions with automatic retries

name: readur
description: Quick, painless, intuitive OCR platform written in Rust and TypeScript. Modern UI with modern API, with an emphasis on intuitive user experience.
analysis: Readur is a self-hostable document management system written in Rust (Axum backend) with a React/TypeScript frontend, offering OCR-based text extraction (Tesseract, multi-language), full-text PostgreSQL search, WebDAV/S3/local-folder sync, labels, folder watching, and OIDC/SSO auth. It's aimed at individuals and teams wanting a Paperless-ngx-style document archive with a modern UI, Docker/Helm deployment, and an API-first design with Swagger docs. Actively developed, with dedicated Claude Code review agents in the repo for OCR, storage-sync, and testing workflows.

use_cases.title: Self-host an OCR document archive with full-text search
Sync documents in from WebDAV, S3, or a watched folder
Replace Paperless-ngx with a Rust-backed alternative
Search scanned multi-language documents by content

name: perplexideez
description: Search the web and your self-hosted apps using local AI agents.
analysis: Perplexideez is a self-hosted Perplexity-style AI search app (SvelteKit/TypeScript) that answers queries by searching the web through a SearXNG instance, grounds responses with clickable source citations, and generates follow-up questions, backed by Postgres and either Ollama or OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoints. It targets self-hosters who want multi-user support, SSO/OIDC, shareable search links with access control, and Kubernetes/Docker deployment, distinguishing it from other homelab Perplexity clones by that integration and multi-tenancy focus. Development appears stalled since November 2024 with no further commits.

use_cases.title: Self-host a private, citation-grounded AI search assistant
Give a homelab multi-user access to AI web search with SSO
Wire local Ollama models to a SearXNG-backed search UI
Deploy an AI search app via Helm/Kubernetes manifests

name: wifi-3d-fusion
description: WiFi-3D-Fusion is an open-source research project that leverages WiFi CSI signals and deep learning to estimate 3D human pose, fusing wireless sensing with computer vision techniques for next-generation spatial awareness.
analysis: WiFi-3D-Fusion is a Python research pipeline that turns WiFi CSI/RSSI signals, captured from an ESP32 or a Nexmon-patched adapter, into real-time 3D human pose and motion sensing, fusing device-free wireless sensing with a CNN detector and a Three.js/Open3D live viewer. It bridges to academic projects like Person-in-WiFi-3D and NeRF-squared, and supports training and continuous learning of its own detection models on captured CSI data. Aimed at researchers and hobbyists experimenting with through-wall, device-free human sensing; explicitly labeled research-only, and the repository has had no commits since August 2025.

use_cases.title: Detect and visualize human motion through walls using WiFi signals
Estimate 3D human pose from CSI data with a trained CNN
Build a low-cost ESP32-based WiFi sensing rig

name: QuantAgent
description: Official Repository for QuantHarness
analysis: QuantHarness (forked here as QuantAgent) is a research multi-agent trading-analysis system built with LangChain/LangGraph, coordinating Indicator, Pattern, Trend, and Decision agents that read K-line charts and technical indicators (RSI, MACD, Stochastic) to produce LONG/SHORT trade recommendations with entry/exit/stop-loss levels. It ships a Flask web interface plus a Python API (TradingGraph), supports Claude, GPT, Qwen, and MiniMax as the underlying LLM, and comes from an academic paper (Stony Brook/CMU/Yale/Fudan) with published benchmarks - intended for researchers and quant-curious developers, not production trading.

use_cases.title: Get an LLM-generated LONG/SHORT trade call from live K-line data
Run a multi-agent chart-pattern and trend analysis pipeline
Swap in Claude, Qwen, or MiniMax as the trading-agent LLM backend
Reproduce or extend the QuantHarness academic benchmark results

name: n8n-skills
description: n8n skillset for Claude Code to build flawless n8n workflows
analysis: n8n-skills is a Claude Code plugin bundling 14 expert skills plus an always-on router and hook-based enforcement layer that teach Claude how to build correct n8n automation workflows using the companion n8n-mcp MCP server. It covers expression syntax, MCP tool usage, workflow patterns, validation-error interpretation, node configuration, JavaScript/Python code nodes, error handling, binary data, sub-workflows, AI agent nodes, multi-instance targeting, and end-to-end self-hosted n8n deployment (Docker Compose + Caddy). It targets developers using Claude Code/Codex to build or operate n8n workflow automations who want to avoid common MCP and node-configuration pitfalls.

use_cases.title: Have Claude Code build correct n8n workflows via the n8n-mcp server
Debug n8n validation errors and expression syntax mistakes
Design an n8n AI Agent node with tools, memory, and structured output
Deploy a production self-hosted n8n instance behind Caddy with HTTPS

name: OpenSpec
description: Spec-driven development (SDD) for AI coding assistants.
analysis: OpenSpec is a spec-driven-development CLI and slash-command workflow (`/opsx:explore`, `/opsx:propose`, `/opsx:apply`, `/opsx:archive`) that gets AI coding assistants and humans to agree on plain-Markdown specs before code is written, storing proposals/specs/design/tasks per change under an `openspec/` folder. It supports 30+ AI tools (Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, etc.), an optional cross-repo 'Stores' feature for shared team specs, and is installed globally via npm. A widely adopted, actively maintained lightweight alternative to heavier spec frameworks like GitHub's Spec Kit.

use_cases.title: Get an AI coding assistant to agree on a spec before writing code
Track in-flight feature proposals as versioned Markdown changes
Share specs across repos on a team via OpenSpec Stores

name: self.so
description: LinkedIn -> personal site generator
analysis: Self is an open-source Next.js web app that turns an uploaded resume/LinkedIn PDF into a published personal website, using Together.ai's Kimi K2.6 model for structured extraction and Llama Guard for safety checks. It uses Clerk for auth, S3 for storage, Upstash Redis as its DB, and Braintrust for LLM tracing, targeting individuals who want an instant personal site without manual site-building. Actively maintained, with tests around resume-generation accuracy.

use_cases.title: Turn a resume PDF into a hosted personal website
Self-host a LinkedIn-to-portfolio generator

name: airgapped-offfline-rag
description: Secure, locally-run Retrieval-Augmented Generation system for document-based question-answering, utilizing Llama 3, Mistral, and Gemini models with a user-friendly Streamlit interface.
analysis: Airgapped Offline RAG is a Streamlit application for document question-answering that runs entirely locally, using quantized GGUF models (Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma) via llama.cpp, LangChain for orchestration, and ChromaDB/Qdrant for vector storage. It targets privacy-conscious users or air-gapped environments who want to upload PDFs and ask questions without any cloud dependency. The stack is Docker-deployable and supports streaming responses, though several features (multi-modal docs, REST API, observability) remain on the roadmap.

use_cases.title: Ask questions over local PDFs without internet access
Run a self-hosted document QA tool for sensitive data
Compare quantized local LLMs (Llama, Mistral, Gemma) for RAG

name: fastsdcpu
description: Fast stable diffusion on CPU and AI PC
analysis: FastSD CPU is a fast Stable Diffusion implementation optimized to run on CPUs and Intel AI PCs (using OpenVINO, LCM, and Adversarial Diffusion Distillation), offering a Qt desktop GUI, an advanced web UI, and a CLI, plus a REST API and MCP server for integration with tools like Claude Desktop and Open WebUI. It targets users without discrete GPUs who want fast (sub-second on a Core i7) text-to-image, image-to-image, ControlNet, LoRA, and upscaling workflows, supporting FLUX, SDXL, and SDXL Turbo/Lightning models in GGUF and safetensors formats. Runs on Windows, Linux, Mac, and even Android/Termux.

use_cases.title: Generate images fast on CPU without a discrete GPU
Run text-to-image locally via an MCP server
Do ControlNet-guided image generation with LoRA models
Upscale and restore images with AuraSR/EDSR

name: BrowserAI
description: Run local LLMs like llama, deepseek-distill, kokoro and more inside your browser
analysis: BrowserAI is a TypeScript SDK that runs LLMs, speech recognition, TTS, and audio source separation entirely client-side in the browser using WebGPU, with pluggable MLC, Transformers.js, Flare (GGUF/WASM), and Demucs engines. It gives web developers a simple API (loadModel/generateText/transcribeAudio/textToSpeech) for private, serverless AI features that run offline after the initial model download, targeting models like Llama, DeepSeek-distill, Whisper, and Kokoro TTS. It is aimed at front-end developers and privacy-conscious teams building AI features without backend inference infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Run a chat LLM fully client-side in a web app with no backend
Add browser-based speech-to-text transcription with Whisper
Add offline text-to-speech using Kokoro in a web app
Separate vocals/drums/bass from an audio track in-browser

name: everything-claude-code
description: The agent harness performance optimization system. Skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor and beyond.
analysis: ECC (everything-claude-code) is a large-scale agent-harness operating system for Claude Code and other coding agents (Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed, GitHub Copilot), providing 68 specialized subagents, 285 skills, 94 legacy command shims, hooks, persistent memory, continuous learning, and AgentShield security scanning across prompts/hooks/MCP config/secrets. Installed as a Claude Code plugin (`/plugin install ecc@ecc`) or via npm packages (ecc-universal, ecc-agentshield), it enforces a plan-test-implement-review-verify-remember-improve loop so agents follow a consistent engineering process instead of ad hoc prompting. Extremely popular (240k+ stars) and actively developed by a single maintainer with a paid Pro tier for private-repo hosting.

use_cases.title: Equip Claude Code with a large curated library of skills and subagents
Enforce a plan-test-implement-review loop on every agent task
Scan agent prompts, hooks, and MCP configs for security issues
Give a coding agent persistent memory and continuous learning across sessions

name: terraform-genai-knowledge-base
description: Fine tune an LLM model to answer questions from your documents.
analysis: A Google Cloud Platform-maintained Terraform module that stands up an end-to-end generative-AI knowledge-base pipeline: Document AI OCR extracts text from uploaded documents, Vertex AI generates question/answer pairs stored in Firestore, results are indexed in Vector Search, and the QA pairs feed fine-tuning of a Vertex AI LLM. It's for platform/infra engineers who want a deployable reference architecture (published to the Terraform Registry) rather than application code, wiring together Cloud Functions, Firestore, Document AI, and Vertex AI via HCL. Actively maintained with dependabot/renovate and periodic CI.

use_cases.title: Deploy a GCP knowledge-base pipeline with Terraform
Auto-generate a fine-tuning dataset from document text via Vertex AI
Provision Document AI OCR plus Vector Search infrastructure as code

name: social-media-scraping-apis
description: A curated collection of social media scraping APIs and tools for Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, and more. Extract posts, profiles, videos, comments, and engagement metrics.
analysis: A thin curated list pointing to third-party scraping APIs and Apify actors for extracting posts, profiles, videos, comments, and engagement metrics from Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, TikTok, YouTube, and Facebook. It appears to be a promotional/lead-gen repo tied to a paid course (skool.com link) with almost no original code — just README content, a follow-creator prompt, and a small script to fetch Apify actor listings. No substantive implementation or documentation was found beyond the top-level tree.

use_cases.title: Find a third-party API for scraping a specific social platform
Browse Apify actors for social media data extraction

note: Social media research & strategy tool — curated scraping/data APIs for audience, competitor and content research.

name: Jarvis-Desktop-Voice-Assistant
description: A python based desktop voice assistant capable of executing system-level commands, integrating speech recognition and text-to-speech, and handling asynchronous user interactions.
analysis: A small, largely single-file Python desktop voice assistant ('Jarvis') that uses speech recognition and text-to-speech to greet the user, launch apps/websites, search Google/Wikipedia, play music, take screenshots, and jot notes. It's a beginner/educational project rather than an LLM-backed agent — simple rule-based command matching, no generative AI involved. Good starting point for learners exploring speech I/O and desktop automation in Python.

use_cases.title: Learn how to build a basic Python voice assistant
Automate simple desktop tasks with voice commands

name: llm-god
description: Desktop app to multi-prompt ChatGPT, Gemini and more at the same time!
analysis: LLM-God is a Windows-first Electron desktop app that embeds multiple LLM chat web interfaces (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Grok, DeepSeek, Copilot) as browser views side by side, letting a user broadcast one prompt to all of them at once via Ctrl+Enter and paste text or screenshots into a shared input. It works by JavaScript-injecting into each provider's web UI (login required per service) rather than calling any API, so it's a productivity wrapper, not an LLM client library. Aimed at individuals who want to quickly compare answers across multiple chat providers without copy-pasting between browser tabs.

use_cases.title: Compare answers from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude side by side
Broadcast one prompt to several AI chat web UIs at once
Paste a screenshot into multiple LLM chats simultaneously

name: Multi-AI-Agent-Systems-with-crewAI
description: Master the art of designing and organizing AI agents. Learn to automate complex, multi-step business processes by creating specialized AI agent teams using the open-source library crewAI.
analysis: This is the notebook set for DeepLearning.AI's 'Multi AI Agent Systems with crewAI' short course, taught by CrewAI founder João Moura, covering role-playing agents, memory, tools, and cooperation patterns (sequential, parallel, hierarchical) using the open-source crewAI library. Each lesson notebook builds a business-process crew — research/writing, customer support, outreach, event planning, financial analysis, resume tailoring — as a worked example rather than a reusable library. It's course material for developers learning multi-agent design, unmaintained since 2024 (course content is static by nature).

use_cases.title: Learn crewAI's role/goal/backstory pattern via worked notebooks
Copy a multi-agent business-process example (support, outreach, event planning)
See sequential vs hierarchical agent crew orchestration examples

name: nof1.ai-alpha-arena
description: nof1.ai Trading Bot is an open-source autonomous trading system built by Nof1.ai as part of the Alpha Arena experiment. It trades real crypto on Hyperliquid using deep reinforcement learning, live market signals, and adaptive AI-driven strategy optimization.
analysis: An open-source autonomous crypto trading bot that connects to any LLM (GPT, DeepSeek, Qwen, Gemini, Grok, Claude) to trade on Hyperliquid, with a Streamlit-style GUI dashboard, multi-model 'collective intelligence' voting, risk management, and copy-trading features. Positioned as part of the 'Alpha Arena' experiment comparing different AI models' trading performance. Very low adoption (7 stars, 1 fork) and distributed as a Windows .exe loader rather than source-run instructions, which alongside inconsistent commit dates suggests an unverified, low-maturity side project.

use_cases.title: Run a local autonomous crypto trading bot
Compare multiple LLM trading strategies head to head

name: octopus
description: One Hub All LLMs For You | 为个人打造的 LLM API 聚合网关
analysis: Octopus is a self-hosted Go/TypeScript gateway that aggregates multiple LLM provider channels (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, etc.) behind one API, converting between OpenAI Chat/Responses and Anthropic message formats, syncing model pricing, and tracking usage analytics through a web admin panel. It's built for individuals who want to point tools like Claude Code, Codex, or OpenAI-SDK clients at a single local endpoint that fans out to many upstream LLM accounts and keys. Supports SQLite/MySQL/Postgres and ships as a Docker image or single Go binary.

use_cases.title: Route Claude Code or Codex traffic through a self-hosted multi-provider gateway
Aggregate several LLM provider API keys behind one endpoint
Track token usage and cost across LLM providers

name: Claude-Code-Board
description: Use Claude Code on Kanban WebUI
analysis: Claude Code Board is a self-hosted Node.js/React web dashboard for managing multiple concurrent Claude Code CLI sessions, offering session creation, work-item/project organization, workflow-stage templates, agent selection from ~/.claude/agents, and real-time WebSocket chat with running sessions. It targets Windows developers who juggle several Claude Code projects at once and want a visual alternative to multiple terminal windows. The author has explicitly marked the project no longer maintained, and it ships with no encryption or real auth, warning it is for personal, local use only.

use_cases.title: Run and monitor multiple Claude Code sessions from one web UI
Organize Claude Code work by project and work item
Assign custom agent personas per workflow stage

name: stenoai
description: Steno is the highly secure privacy-first AI notepad & notetaker for all your confidential conversations. On Windows & MacOS. For government and defence sectors.
analysis: Steno (stenoai) is a privacy-first, 100% on-device macOS (and alpha Windows) desktop app that records, live-transcribes with speaker labels, summarizes, and lets you query meetings using local AI models (Parakeet TDT v3 for live transcription, Whisper for other languages, Gemma/Qwen via Ollama for summarization), with no cloud dependency by default. It supports auto-detecting meeting start/stop, system audio capture without Screen Recording permission, Markdown export, Obsidian sync, custom report templates, and optional bring-your-own-cloud-model (OpenAI/Anthropic/Bedrock), plus agent skills (`/steno`, `granola-to-steno`) for querying notes from Claude Code. It targets government, defense, legal, healthcare, and privacy-conscious professionals who need confidential meeting notes that never leave their machine.

use_cases.title: Record and transcribe confidential meetings entirely on-device
Ask natural-language questions across your meeting history
Sync meeting notes into an Obsidian vault as Markdown
Query Steno meeting notes from Claude Code via the /steno agent skill

name: tentix
description: TenTix (10x Efficiency) - An AI native customer service platform with 10x accelerated resolution. Support MCP extension, and AI knowlage base system.
analysis: Tentix is an open-source AI-native customer service and ticketing platform (TypeScript, Bun) that pairs a support-ticket system with a LangGraph AI agent doing RAG over a unified PostgreSQL+pgvector knowledge base (starred conversations, historical tickets, general docs), configurable handoff and MCP-style workflow nodes, and Feishu notifications. Aimed at teams wanting a self-hosted, AI-accelerated helpdesk with an admin knowledge-base UI and a visual React Flow workflow editor for the AI agent's behavior.

use_cases.title: Self-host an AI-assisted customer support ticketing system
Build a RAG knowledge base from historical support tickets
Design an agent handoff and escalation workflow visually
Route customer messages to a support agent via Feishu

name: Baiss
analysis: Baiss is a cross-platform desktop AI assistant (Windows, macOS, Linux) built with a .NET 8 / Avalonia UI frontend in Clean Architecture and a Python/FastAPI backend, running local LLMs via llama.cpp with RAG powered by DuckDB and FlashRank re-ranking. It targets privacy-focused developers and researchers who want a local-first chat/RAG assistant without cloud dependencies, with support for multiple AI providers and an extensible plugin architecture. Ships as installable desktop binaries with SQL migrations tracking active feature development.

use_cases.title: Run a private, local-first AI chat assistant on desktop
Reference a Clean Architecture C#/Python hybrid app for AI desktop tools
Build local RAG search over personal documents with DuckDB
Study integrating llama.cpp with a FastAPI backend and native UI

name: CloudGallery
description: CloudGallery is an Android app that lets you instantly back up all your images to Telegram using Bot API — simple, Secure, and infinite.
analysis: Chitralaya CloudGallery is an open-source Android app (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) that backs up phone photos to a user's own Telegram account via the Telegram Bot API, functioning as a free, privacy-first alternative to Google Photos or iCloud. Bot tokens and chat IDs are stored in the Android keystore, and a local (and Telegram-backed) JSON metadata database tracks synced images for browsing and cross-device restore. It targets individual privacy-conscious users wanting unlimited photo backup without a company-run cloud, and is a solo-developer, community-supported project that intentionally lacks advanced features like sharing links, multi-user support, or end-to-end encryption.

use_cases.title: Back up phone photos privately using your own Telegram bot
Avoid Google Photos or iCloud by self-managing cloud storage
Reference a Jetpack Compose Android app with local database sync

name: money-Ai-agents
description: Lucid Agents Commerce SDK. Bootstrap AI agents in 60 seconds that can pay, sell, and participate in agentic commerce supply chains. Our protocol agnostic SDK provides CLI-generated templates and drop-in adapters for Hono, Express, Next.js, and TanStack, giving you instant access to crypto/fiat payment rails (AP2, A2A, x402, ERC8004).
analysis: Lucid Agents (repo name money-Ai-agents) is a TypeScript-first, protocol-agnostic framework and CLI for building and monetizing AI agents, with native support for x402 payments, A2A agent-to-agent communication, and ERC-8004 onchain identity. It's a composable monorepo — a protocol-agnostic core runtime plus optional extensions (http, payments, wallets, identity, a2a, ap2) and framework adapters (Hono, Express, Next.js, TanStack) — letting a developer scaffold a paid agent with `bunx @lucid-agents/cli` and accept USDC on Base or Solana out of the box. It targets developers experimenting with agentic commerce and agent marketplaces; the low star/fork count and thin adoption signal an early-stage, still-maturing project rather than production infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Scaffold a paid AI agent that accepts USDC crypto payments in minutes
Build an agent marketplace where agents discover and pay each other for services
Register onchain identity and reputation for an autonomous agent
Track incoming/outgoing agent payments with exportable analytics for accounting

name: clawdis
description: Your own personal AI assistant. Talk via WhatsApp, Telegram or Web.
analysis: Clawdis is a self-hosted personal AI assistant with a TypeScript Gateway control plane (WebSocket/TCP) that connects a Pi agent runtime to multiple surfaces: WhatsApp, Telegram, WebChat, a macOS menu-bar app with voice wake and push-to-talk, and paired iOS/Android nodes with a live Canvas UI. It supports browser control, cron/scheduling, group chat activation rules, and Gmail-triggered wake hooks, aiming to be a single-user, local-first assistant that feels always-on across devices. The repository has almost no external adoption (4 stars) and shows no commit activity beyond its initial push.

use_cases.title: Run a self-hosted AI assistant reachable via WhatsApp and Telegram
Add voice wake and push-to-talk to a personal agent on macOS
Pair a phone as a remote node for camera/screen agent commands
Trigger an agent workflow from an incoming Gmail message

name: ingest
description: Parse files (e.g. code repos) and websites to clipboard or a file for ingestions by AI / LLMs
analysis: Ingest is a Go CLI that walks a directory of source code (or crawls a website or PDF) and flattens it into a single markdown or JSON prompt suitable for feeding to an LLM, with include/exclude glob filtering, git diff/log inclusion, Tree-sitter-based code compression, offline or Anthropic-API token counting, and optional direct hand-off to any OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint. It targets developers who want to quickly build LLM context from a codebase or web page without manual copy-pasting, and ships as a single Go binary with shell completions. Actively maintained with recent commits and GitHub Actions release automation.

use_cases.title: Turn a code repo into a single LLM-ready markdown prompt
Crawl a website into markdown for LLM ingestion
Count and estimate tokens for a codebase before sending it to an LLM
Compress source files with Tree-sitter to save context tokens

name: obsidian-claude-pkm
description: A complete starter kit for an Obsidian + Claude Code personal knowledge management system.
analysis: This is a complete starter kit that turns an Obsidian vault into an AI-driven personal knowledge management and accountability system powered by Claude Code. It wires a goal cascade (3-year vision to yearly/monthly/weekly goals to daily notes) together with Claude Code skills (/daily, /weekly, /monthly, /project, /adopt) and four specialized subagents (goal-aligner, weekly-reviewer, note-organizer, inbox-processor) that carry cross-session memory. It's aimed at Obsidian users who want their notes, goals, and daily tasks kept in sync automatically via bash hooks and zero external dependencies, and it supports both fresh vaults and adopting an existing one.

use_cases.title: Set up an Obsidian vault where Claude Code manages daily and weekly reviews
Connect long-term goals to daily tasks with an automated goal cascade
Retrofit Claude Code skills and agents onto an existing Obsidian vault
Use an AI accountability coach output style to stay aligned with goals

name: system-design-visualizer
description: An interactive tool that transforms static system design diagrams into explorable, interactive visualizations using AI.
analysis: System Design Visualizer is a React/Vite web app that turns a static system-design image (architecture diagram, flowchart) into an interactive, explorable graph: it uses OpenAI GPT-4o vision to convert the uploaded image into an editable Mermaid.js diagram, then renders it as a React Flow graph where clicking a node (load balancer, database, etc.) surfaces AI-inferred details like tech stack and role. It targets engineers and architects who want to explore or document existing system diagrams interactively rather than as flat images, and includes a mock mode that works without an OpenAI API key. Development has been quiet since its initial release in December 2025.

use_cases.title: Upload a system architecture screenshot and get an editable Mermaid diagram
Click through an interactive system design graph to see component details

name: openagi
description: Paving the way for open agents and AGI for all.
analysis: OpenAGI is a Python framework for building autonomous, human-like multi-agent systems, structured around an Admin agent that assigns Worker agents (with roles, instructions, and tool actions) using a TaskPlanner for manual or fully autonomous task decomposition, plus optional long-term memory for cross-session recall. It supports multiple LLM backends (OpenAI, Gemini) and pluggable tools like DuckDuckGo/Tavily search, targeting developers who want a lower-level building-block library rather than a polished product. Development has stalled since February 2025, with no recent commits despite moderate community interest (623 stars).

use_cases.title: Build an Admin/Worker multi-agent hierarchy for a task pipeline
Give agents long-term memory across conversations
Prototype autonomous task decomposition with a TaskPlanner

name: local-voice-ai
description: Local voice AI powered by llama-cpp, Kokoro, Nemotron STT, and LiveKit.
analysis: A self-hosted, real-time local voice AI assistant that runs STT, LLM, and TTS entirely in one Docker container, supervised by a single Python parent process: llama.cpp (default Gemma model) for the LLM, Nemotron or faster-whisper for speech-to-text, Kokoro for text-to-speech, and LiveKit Agents/WebRTC for the real-time pipeline, fronted by a Next.js frontend. Any component can be swapped for a cloud provider (OpenAI, LiveKit Cloud, remote STT/TTS) via a base-URL environment variable. Aimed at developers who want a private, offline-capable voice assistant runnable on a single machine, with documented GPU (NVIDIA) and Apple Silicon (Metal) paths.

use_cases.title: Run a fully local, private real-time voice assistant
Prototype a LiveKit-based voice agent with swappable providers
Deploy a single-container STT+LLM+TTS stack

name: MCP-Defender
description: Desktop app that automatically scans and blocks malicious MCP traffic in AI apps like Cursor, Claude, VS Code and Windsurf.
analysis: MCP Defender is an Electron desktop app that transparently proxies all Model Context Protocol traffic between AI apps (Cursor, Claude, VS Code, Windsurf) and MCP servers, scanning requests and responses against a signature set to detect and block malicious tool calls such as command injection, SSH key leaks, and path traversal. It targets developers and security teams worried about supply-chain risk in the growing MCP tool ecosystem. The project was acquired by Docker in mid-2026, so this standalone repo now appears to be in maintenance/wind-down mode rather than active independent development.

use_cases.title: Detect and block malicious MCP tool call traffic
Audit which MCP servers an AI app is actually calling

name: Kylie
description: Whatsap Agent
analysis: Kylie is a WhatsApp-integrated AI companion agent built with LangGraph, receiving text, voice notes, and images via the WhatsApp Cloud API and responding in kind (Groq LLM for text, ElevenLabs TTS, Whisper STT, Google Vision, FLUX image generation). It's a personal/hobbyist tutorial project demonstrating multimodal agent design: a router node dispatches between conversation, image, audio, calendar-tool, and web-search branches, with short-term SQLite state and long-term Qdrant vector memory. Development appears to have stopped shortly after the initial release (created and last pushed within days of each other in November 2025).

use_cases.title: Study a LangGraph multimodal agent architecture example
Build a WhatsApp bot with voice notes and image responses
See a reference implementation of short/long-term agent memory

name: wifi-densepose
description: π RuView turns commodity WiFi signals into real-time spatial intelligence, vital sign monitoring, and presence detection — all without a single pixel of video.
analysis: RuView (WiFi DensePose) is a Rust-based edge platform that turns Channel State Information from cheap ESP32 sensors into spatial intelligence: presence/occupancy detection, contactless breathing and heart-rate monitoring, fall detection, camera-free pose estimation, and room/environment mapping, all without cameras or wearables. It integrates natively with Home Assistant, Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and Matter, ships pretrained models on Hugging Face, and includes a large catalog of edge 'cog' modules plus an AI-agent operator harness (Claude/Codex) for calibration and verification. Aimed at smart-home and IoT builders wanting privacy-preserving, camera-free sensing running fully on local edge hardware.

Integrate WiFi-based occupancy sensing into Home Assistant
Run camera-free pose estimation from WiFi CSI data
Build fall-detection or sleep-monitoring automations locally

name: agentic_coding_flywheel_setup
description: Bootstraps a fresh Ubuntu VPS into a complete multi-agent AI development environment in 30 minutes: coding agents, session management, safety tools, and coordination infrastructure
analysis: Agentic Coding Flywheel Setup (ACFS) is a one-liner curl-to-bash installer that turns a fresh Ubuntu VPS into a fully configured multi-agent AI coding environment in about 30 minutes. It installs and wires up three coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI), a modern shell (zsh/oh-my-zsh/p10k), language runtimes, and a suite of agent-coordination utilities (NTM, MCP Agent Mail, SLB) plus an onboarding curriculum for beginners. It is manifest-driven (a single YAML source of truth generates installer scripts and doctor checks) and ships an accompanying wizard website for non-technical users to rent a VPS and SSH in. Aimed at solo builders and small teams who want a reproducible, idempotent agentic-coding VPS without hand-configuring tools one by one.

Standardize a team's agentic dev environment so every box is identical
Onboard a non-technical beginner to agent-assisted coding via a guided wizard
Wire up coordination tooling (NTM, MCP Agent Mail) for multiple agents working in parallel

Bundle agents and skills into a plugin for a workflow

name: paperai
description: 📄 🤖 AI for medical and scientific papers
analysis: paperai is a Python application for bulk AI-driven analysis of medical and scientific papers, built on the txtai embeddings/RAG library plus a SQLite article store, generating Markdown/CSV reports and PDF annotations from LLM-answered questions over a paper corpus. It's aimed at researchers who need to run hundreds of structured queries (e.g. 'sample size', 'list possible causes') across large literature sets rather than reading papers manually, with entry points for indexing, single queries, an interactive shell, and full report generation. name: mcp
description: Google 💚 MCP
analysis: This is Google's official index of Model Context Protocol servers and guidance for using them, listing both Google-managed remote MCP endpoints (BigQuery, Cloud SQL, GKE, Spanner, and more) and open-source MCP servers (Workspace, Firebase, Cloud Run, gcloud CLI, security tooling) that can run locally or be deployed to Cloud Run/GKE. name: quint-code
description: Engineering decisions engine that know when they're stale. Frame, compare, decide — with evidence decay and parity enforcement. For Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex and more.

It targets developers using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and similar agents who want durable, auditable engineering decisions with staleness/drift detection, delivered as a Go CLI/MCP server (`haft`) with per-host skill and instruction-file integration and a local SQLite-backed decision ledger.

Wire a durable MCP memory/governance layer into Claude Code or Codex
