name: promptfx
description: Kotlin LLM Prompts and User Interface
analysis: PromptFx is a Kotlin prototype for LLM prompt engineering and chaining (the promptkt/promptex libraries) paired with a JavaFX demo UI for testing OpenAI- and Gemini-compatible models: document Q&A/RAG over local PDFs, prompt template/scripting tools, translation/summarization/sentiment views, and image/audio playgrounds. The promptex module adds an execution layer with agent, tool, and pipeline logic plus an MCP server/client. The README explicitly frames it as built for demonstration and exploration rather than production use, aimed at JVM developers experimenting with prompt engineering and RAG patterns outside the Python ecosystem.

use_cases.title: Experiment with prompt templates and chaining in a desktop JVM app
Run local document Q&A over a folder of PDFs
Prototype an MCP server or client from Kotlin

name: AI-Tutorial-Codes-Included
description: Multi-agent systems, memory, planning, reasoning loops
analysis: A massive, continuously growing collection of Jupyter notebooks and Python scripts from Marktechpost's tutorial site, covering agentic AI, multi-agent systems, memory, planning, RAG, adversarial attacks, and dozens of specific frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, smolagents, MCP, etc). Each item pairs a runnable Colab notebook with a published how-to article, aimed at developers learning current AI-agent techniques through worked examples rather than a cohesive library. It is essentially a running index of applied AI-agent tutorials, not a maintained product.

use_cases.title: Find a worked example for a specific agentic-AI technique
Copy a Colab notebook as a starting point for a new agent prototype
Survey current agent frameworks and patterns via curated examples

name: autogen
description: A programming framework for agentic AI
analysis: AutoGen is Microsoft Research's framework for building multi-agent AI applications, offering a layered Core API (message passing, event-driven agents), a simpler AgentChat API for common multi-agent chat patterns, and Extensions for LLM providers, tool use, and code execution, plus AutoGen Studio (a no-code GUI) and AutoGen Bench for evaluation. It targets Python (and .NET) developers building multi-agent systems with MCP tool integration and orchestration patterns like two-agent chat or group chats. The project is now officially in maintenance mode, with Microsoft directing new projects to its successor, Microsoft Agent Framework.

use_cases.title: Prototype a multi-agent chat workflow with AgentChat API
Build agents that call MCP servers as tools
Use AutoGen Studio's no-code GUI to test agent workflows

name: LLMs-from-scratch
description: Implement a ChatGPT-like LLM in PyTorch from scratch, step by step
analysis: The official companion code repository for Sebastian Raschka's book 'Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)', walking through implementing, pretraining, and finetuning a GPT-like LLM in PyTorch chapter by chapter (attention mechanisms, KV cache, GQA, LoRA finetuning, instruction tuning). It's organized as Jupyter notebooks plus supporting Python scripts per chapter and appendix, designed to run on a laptop without specialized hardware. Aimed at developers/ML learners who want hands-on understanding of LLM internals rather than a production training framework; extremely popular (100k+ stars) and actively maintained alongside a video course and a sequel book on reasoning models.

use_cases.title: Learn how GPT-style LLMs are built layer by layer
Reference PyTorch code for pretraining a small LLM
Study LoRA finetuning and instruction-tuning examples

name: awesome-llm-apps
description: 100+ AI Agents, Agent Skills and RAG Apps - Free and Open Source.
analysis: Awesome LLM Apps is a huge, actively maintained collection of 100+ hand-built, end-to-end open-source AI agents, Claude/Codex/Cursor agent skills, and RAG apps organized into categories (starter agents, multi-agent teams, always-on agents, voice agents, agent skills). Each entry is a runnable, self-contained example (Python/Streamlit apps or `npx skills add` installable skills) covering use cases like travel planning, fraud investigation, legal research, and financial analysis, built on frameworks like OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, AG2, and ADK. It targets developers and solo builders who want copy-paste-ready agent implementations or new coding-agent skills rather than a framework to learn from scratch. It is extremely popular (130k+ stars), updated weekly with new templates, and CI-gated with security/eval checks.

use_cases.title: Clone a working single-file AI agent app to bootstrap a new project idea
Install a Claude Code skill in seconds via npx skills add
Study a reference multi-agent team implementation (finance, legal, recruitment)
Find an always-on agent pattern for scheduled monitoring and briefings

name: CodeMazeGuides
description: The main repository for all the Code Maze guides
analysis: CodeMazeGuides is the code-sample repository backing the Code Maze .NET blog, containing hundreds of small, self-contained ASP.NET Core / .NET solutions (one folder per article) covering topics like background services, MVC controllers, EF Core, and web API patterns. It is primarily a reference collection for C#/.NET developers to browse working examples tied to specific blog posts and tutorials rather than a single cohesive application. It is very actively maintained, with new example projects added continuously and CI validating each solution builds.

use_cases.title: Find a working ASP.NET Core example for a specific pattern like background services or MVC
Follow along with a Code Maze blog tutorial using the matching solution folder
Copy a minimal reproducible .NET project as a starting point for a new feature

name: PowerApps-Samples
description: Sample code for Power Apps, including Dataverse, model-driven apps, canvas apps, Power Apps component framework, portals, and AI Builder.
analysis: This is Microsoft's official sample-code repository for the Power Platform, covering Dataverse, model-driven apps, canvas apps, the Power Apps Component Framework (PCF), Power Pages portals, and AI Builder. It is a large, well-organized reference collection (mostly C# and TypeScript) of runnable examples that Power Platform developers copy from or learn architecture patterns against, rather than a single cohesive product. It is actively maintained by Microsoft with continuous updates and CLA-gated community contributions.

use_cases.title: Find a working PCF control sample to base a custom Power Apps component on
Learn Dataverse API patterns from official Microsoft sample code
Copy an AI Builder starter kit for invoice or document processing

name: Dynamics365-Apps-Samples
description: Sample code for Dynamics 365 apps
analysis: This is Microsoft's official sample-code repository for Dynamics 365 apps (Customer Service, Contact Center, and more), containing C#/JavaScript SDK samples such as closing incidents, scheduling resources, and channel-integration frameworks like a Twilio call-center integration. It's aimed at enterprise developers extending Dynamics 365/Dataverse solutions and serves purely as reference code tied to Microsoft's official documentation, not a reusable library or standalone app.

use_cases.title: Look up a working C# sample for a Dynamics 365 SDK task
Reference a channel-integration pattern for Customer Service

name: D365WebApi
description: Javascript libary for Dynamics CRM Web API
analysis: D365WebApi is a small JavaScript library for calling the Dynamics 365 / Dynamics CRM Web API from form scripts and web resources, inspired by SDK.REST.js and using superagent.js for HTTP requests and q.js for promises. It is meant for Dynamics 365 developers who need a thin promise-based wrapper over the Web API without pulling in a full SDK. The upstream project (WebAPI.REST.js by Kimlv) has had no commits since 2016 and this fork has zero stars, indicating it is effectively unmaintained.

use_cases.title: Call Dynamics 365 Web API from a form script with promises
Reference a lightweight alternative to the full Dynamics SDK

name: Xrm.Tools.CRMWebAPI
description: This is an API helper for working with the Common Data Service (CDS)  Web API
analysis: Xrm.Tools.CRMWebAPI is a lightweight API helper library for the Dynamics 365 / Common Data Service Web API, with near-identical implementations across .NET, JavaScript/Node, Python, and PHP so developers can write consistent CRUD/metadata code regardless of platform. It's aimed at Dynamics 365/Power Platform developers integrating with CRM data from web resources or external applications, designed to interoperate with Azure Active Directory auth without baking it in. No commits since December 2022, so it's effectively unmaintained.

use_cases.title: Call the Dynamics 365 Web API from a JavaScript web resource
Build a .NET integration against Common Data Service data
Share consistent CRM API code across multiple languages
